## An action count I could not measure statically, three times over (2026-10-13)

Checking a numeric claim in this file, which says **27** actions in one entry and
**36** in another. Three attempts, each a different instance of the trap this
file records most often:

1. `ast.Call` with `func.attr == "SimpleAction"` matched **zero** - the code is
   `Gio.SimpleAction.new("quit", None)`, a `.new()` call, not a constructor.
2. Accepting `new_stateful` as well gave **29** - and the seven still missing are
   the strip's chips, which **work**, because they are built in a `for` loop from
   a tuple, so the action's name is a **variable** and no literal exists.
3. So **a static AST scan cannot answer this question at all.** The test that
   drives `_create_actions()` and records what `add_action` received is the only
   valid instrument, and it agrees with the **36**.

**A scan that finds nothing is not a finding**, and a scan that finds *some* is
worse, because the number it prints is right. Three of the four runs printed a
plausible figure (0, 27, 29) and every one was an artefact of the pattern.

## The wizard's "fill the void" mark was drawn on top of the text it was meant to sit under (2026-10-13)

The void-mark fix - *"The void now carries Chronoa's orb"* - was never rendered,
because the 17 `setup:*` pages had **never once been rendered in this
repository's history**. The first sweep of them found it.

**Measured on `setup:extras`, not eyeballed.** The mark's blue pixels occupy
**y=705..798, x=593..686**. The row-card borders on that page fall at y=**693**,
**748** and **803**, so the mark was drawn across **two** of them, covering the
word "speaker" in *"Who said what - split a recording by speaker"* - with **824
near-white text pixels** immediately to its left. The page's layout is correct
(`test_ui_layout_contract.py` is 16 passed; no wizard page asks for a sideways
scrollbar), so the only thing wrong was a decoration painted on top of the page.

**Cause: `_void_has_room` asked whether the content scrolls, which is a different
question from whether there is space to put something in.**

```python
return adjustment.get_upper() <= adjustment.get_page_size() + 1
```

A page whose content ended **six pixels** above the window answered "yes, there
is a void", and a **112px** mark was drawn centred over the last rows. The mark's
size is now read out of the SVG it is drawn from (`MARK_PX`, derived rather than
typed so redrawing it cannot leave a threshold below it) and the gap has to hold
it.

**And the gap has to be measured off the content, not off the adjustment — which
the first version of the fix got wrong in the other direction.** `upper` is the
*allocated* height of the scrolled child, and that child is an `Adw.Clamp` with
`vexpand`, so it is handed the whole viewport and reports `upper == page_size`
**whatever its contents measure**. Thresholding on `upper` therefore removed the
mark from `setup:brain`, whose two lines of text leave roughly 500px of obvious
void.

**That over-fit was caught by rendering the two pages, not by a test** - the 46
wizard tests were green throughout, before and after, and the existing
`_void_has_room` cases still pass because they pass an adjustment with no
`content_height` and fall back to `upper`. The caller now measures the clamp's
**natural** height and passes the number in, which also keeps `Gtk` out of
module scope (`Gtk` is imported inside `build_window` on purpose - this module is
imported by the MCP server and the CLI).

Verified by rendering, both directions:

| page | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `setup:extras` | mark **over two row cards**, 5,839 px | **mark absent** |
| `setup:brain` | mark present, 5,832 px at y=659..752 | **identical**, 5,832 px at y=659..752 |

**The four failures I got while measuring this were mine.** Running the wizard
suites alongside a concurrent render gave 4 failed / 176 passed in
`test_mode_choice_routes_the_flow.py` and `test_cloud_branch_is_honest.py`; run
without the competing display they are **10 passed**, and in isolation also
passed. That is this file's own concurrency trap - D-Bus names, and now broadway
displays - and it is the **fifth** time this session that concurrency, not the
code, manufactured a failure that looked like a defect.
## The model picker was a dead end on a fresh install, and said so while being one (2026-10-13)

Asked to review the main UI for what a person would actually experience. The
first thing that came out of reading the code was on the path **every** person
walks: opening the app on a machine where nothing is installed.

`gui/model_picker.py`'s rows are built from `local_llm.TIERS`, so a fresh
machine lists all six tiers, each with a download icon and the subtitle
**"not installed - this is a download, not a mode"** - and then:

    row.set_activatable(usable and not active)

`usable` is `spec.key in installed`, so **every row was inert**. Measured: on a
machine with no model, six rows, six instructions to download something, and no
way to press any of them. The picker exists to answer *"which model answers"* and
on a fresh install it answered that and refused to be changed.

**It is worse than a missing row, because the row explains itself.** A download
is not a mode - that part is right, and `app.answer-model` correctly refuses an
uninstalled tier by name. What was wrong was *stopping there*: an instruction
with no way to follow it reads as something the app has already considered and
declined to do, which is the dead-control class this file records in four other
costumes.

The fix routes the press to `common.open_setup` - **the consolidated door** the
three panels with "not installed" rows already use, reached through
`app.activate_action("setup")` so the header button and `Ctrl+Shift+S` stay the
same path. It deliberately does **not** hand the key to `answer-model`: that
would trade a dead end for a correct refusal, which is still a dead end.

**And the press asks `local_llm` rather than trusting the row**, so a download
that finishes while the popover is open switches the model instead of opening the
wizard - the row was drawn before the fact and the click happens after it.

### Three of my own tests were wrong in ways worth recording

1. **`get_sensitive()` is not the inverse of `set_activatable()`.** Measured on
   the installed libadwaita: `set_activatable(False)` leaves `get_sensitive()`
   reading **`True`**, and only `get_activatable()` reads `False`. The first
   version of the regression test used `get_sensitive()`, so **every row passed
   with the dead end fully restored** - the one thing a test written to catch
   dead rows must not be. It is the "a check that cannot fail" trap wearing the
   costume of a control.
2. **A helper that set the machine state hid two tests' own setups.** `_picker`
   forced `installed = set()` and `active = ""`, so
   `test_pressing_an_installed_model_still_switches` switched nothing and
   `test_the_answering_row_is_the_only_one_that_is_inert` found no answering row.
   Both failed for reasons unrelated to what they claim to check. Fixed to read
   the state, and **the next test then failed for the same reason** - it never
   arranged the machine either. **A test that does not set up the machine it
   measures is measuring the fixture**, and I wrote that sentence into the helper
   and then broke it one line later.
3. **`ModelPicker.__new__` cannot build one.** `popdown` is a `Gtk.Popover` vfunc
   and a Python attribute on an *uninitialised* GObject does not shadow it: all
   four new tests failed with *"object ... is not initialized"* before the
   fixture switched to a real construction. `TestTheChoice` documents this trap
   and I walked into it anyway - **a documented trap is still a trap when the
   fixture is the thing doing the constructing.**

And a **pre-existing** test broke for a related reason and was wrong to:
`test_a_pick_hands_the_key_to_the_apps_own_action` picked `qwen3-8b` while its
fixture installed only `qwen3-1.7b`, so it was picking a tier the machine does
not have. Its subject is "a pick of an available model reaches the app's own
action", so it now installs what it picks - the `GSETTINGS_BACKEND` and
`fake_bin` lesson: **a fixture that does not contain the thing the test operates
on is describing a different machine.**

**5 mutations, 5 caught**, the first being the shipped dead end restored
verbatim:

| mutation | |
|---|---|
| `set_activatable(usable and not active)` (**the shipped bug**) | **2 failed** |
| the absent-model route removed | 1 failed |
| the route returns silently | 1 failed |
| every key treated as installed | 1 failed |
| the subtitle stops saying "download" | 1 failed |
## A failed turn was drawn in the assistant's own bubble, reading as its answer (2026-10-13)

The second thing the UI review found, and it is on the path everybody walks when
something goes wrong.

`app/conversation.py`'s `_on_response_ready` had one line for the failure case:

    self.window.set_response(f"Error: {result}")

`set_response` **builds the assistant's turn**. So a Python exception was
appended to the transcript in the assistant's own bubble, in the assistant's
styling, reading as something Chronoa had said:

> **you**  what's the weather
> **Chronoa**  Error: HTTPConnectError(...)

Three consequences, and the first is the visible one. It was not offered for
regeneration, because regeneration is offered on **answers** - so the one turn
that most needed redoing was the one that looked finished. And a person reading
back through a conversation had to work out which of the assistant's turns were
replies and which were crash dumps.

The fix routes it to `add_notice_row(..., "error")` - the same seam the
compaction and cloud notes use, whose own docstring states the rule this broke:
*"a note about the turn, not something the assistant said."*

**`error` is a new kind rather than a reuse of `compaction`, and the reason is
prominence.** Every other notice is housekeeping and is `dim-label` on purpose,
because it should recede behind the reply. A turn that **did not happen** is the
thing a person most needs to see, and dimming it would have made the notice
quieter than the fake bubble it replaced - a fix that is a regression. So the
error row is undimmed, carries `turn-error`, and takes the app's **one** warning
colour `#ef4444` - the same value `.status-attention` already uses, so a person
who has learned it in the status line sees the same signal here. A second red
would be a second thing to learn.

### The marker is added beside `turn-notice`, never instead of it

`_keeps_across_replies` keys on `turn-notice`, which is what lets a note outlive
the turn's text. The error row carries **both** classes. A failure that vanishes
the moment anything else is said in that turn has no value at all.

### Two mutations ran clean, and both were gaps in my own tests

| mutation | first run | what it actually breaks |
|---|---|---|
| the warning icon removed | **survived** | nothing — no test looked at the icon |
| `_keeps_across_replies` repointed from `turn-notice` to `turn-error` | **survived** | **every compaction and cloud note**, silently |

The second is the instructive one. Repointing the predicate at `turn-error`
leaves **every error row working** - which is the only thing this file was
written to check - so it reads as harmless, while the rows that were keeping
that marker alive quietly stop surviving. **A test that checks the new thing does
not check the old thing it shares a mechanism with**, and from inside the new
test the two are indistinguishable.

**7 mutations, 7 caught** after both witnesses were added, including the shipped
defect restored verbatim:

| mutation | |
|---|---|
| `set_response(f"Error: {result}")` (**the shipped bug**) | 1 failed |
| filed as a `compaction` note | 1 failed |
| the error row dimmed like a note | 1 failed |
| the `turn-error` marker removed | 2 failed |
| the `turn-notice` marker dropped | 5 failed |
| the warning icon removed | 1 failed |
| the survival marker repointed at `turn-error` | 1 failed |

### Three harness slips of my own, and the first is the recurring one

1. **`ModelPicker.__new__`** - `popdown` is a `Gtk.Popover` vfunc, and a Python
   attribute on an uninitialised GObject does not shadow it, so all four new
   picker tests failed with *"object ... is not initialized"*.
   `TestTheChoice` documents this trap in full and I walked into it anyway,
   because the fixture was the thing doing the constructing.
2. **`get_sensitive()` is not the inverse of `set_activatable()`.** Measured on
   this libadwaita: `set_activatable(False)` leaves `get_sensitive()` reading
   `True`. The picker's first dead-row test used `get_sensitive()`, so **it
   passed with the dead end fully restored** - the one thing a regression test
   written to catch dead rows must not be.
3. **A helper that set the machine state hid two tests' own setups**, and the
   next test then failed for the same reason because it never arranged the
   machine either. I wrote *"a test that does not set up the machine it
   measures is measuring the fixture"* into the helper's docstring and broke it
   one line later.
## Two messages typed in one turn became two turns, and Stop stopped the wrong one (2026-10-13)

The third thing the UI review found, and the one a person hits by accident
rather than by understanding the app.

`_submit` had no in-flight guard, and **there is no lock anywhere on that
path** - not in `_submit`, not in `assistant.handle`, and the composer is never
disabled. So a message typed while a turn was running started a **second
`handle()` against the same assistant**. Measured with a stand-in `Assistant`:

    handle('first message') started
    handle('second message, typed while the first was running') started
    peak concurrent handle() calls: 2
    the assistant's history now holds: ['first', 'second']

Both turns mutate the same `_history`. But **the history is not the part anyone
sees**, and that is what made this worth fixing rather than noting. `_submit`
reassigns every one of:

| state | what the second turn did to the first |
|---|---|
| `_turn_speech`, `_turn_buffer`, `_turn_streamed` | the running turn's **spoken output went into the second turn's queue** |
| the assistant's turn | the first turn's reply landed **inside the second turn's bubble** |
| `_turn_future` | **Stop stopped whichever turn was submitted last** - the one that had not started |
| `_turn_marks` | the first turn's elapsed clock **restarted**: the wait grew by nothing while the reading went backwards |

Two answers interleaved into one, and a Stop button that pointed the wrong way.

### Queued, not refused - and not run beside it

`window._submit_input` adds the user turn to the transcript **before** it emits
`user-input`. So refusing a second message would leave a question on screen that
Chronoa never answers, which is worse than either alternative. The queue is
FIFO and drains from `_on_response_ready`, on **both** exits.

**The failure exit is the one that would have been missed.** `_on_response_ready`
returns as soon as it has drawn the failure, so draining only at the bottom
strands every queued message - at the exact moment somebody is watching
hardest, where a dead queue reads as the app hanging.

### Cancelled turns never call back, so Stop needs its own line

`AsyncBridge._on_done` **drops a `CancelledError` without invoking the
callback**. So for a stopped turn, the one place that clears the in-flight flag
- `_on_response_ready` - never runs. With no other clear, every message typed
after a Stop is queued behind a turn that no longer exists, **and the queue never
drains again for the life of the process**. `voice.py` now clears it directly.

The queue itself is **kept** across a Stop, in order: stopping twice and then
typing answers the two older messages first, because `_submit` only starts now
when nothing is waiting. A test that made a second voice object reported this
very failure as though the fix were absent - see below.

### `_turn_in_flight` and `_turn_queue` are properties

This is a `Mixin` mixed into `Application` and **nothing runs an initialiser** -
the existing `_turn_*` state is the same, assigned on first use. A plain
attribute would raise `AttributeError` on the very first message typed in a
fresh process. Both read through `getattr` with a default.

**7 mutations, 7 caught**, the first being the shipped bug restored verbatim:

| mutation | |
|---|---|
| the in-flight guard removed (**the shipped bug**) | **4 failed** |
| the queue never drains | 4 failed |
| the queue drained newest-first | 3 failed |
| the **failure** exit stops draining | 1 failed |
| the **success** exit stops draining | 3 failed |
| the turn never marked in flight | 4 failed |
| Stop does not release the flag | 2 failed |

### Two harness faults of mine, and both looked exactly like the bug

1. **Two mixins, two objects.** The Stop test built a *separate* voice object
   and called the handler there, so the flag was cleared on an object the
   conversation never read - and the test failed with **"a stopped turn still
   claims to be running"**, which is the precise failure the fix exists to
   prevent. **Two mixins that are one object in production are two objects in a
   test** unless the test says otherwise. Driving
   `VoiceMixin._stop_speaking(mixin, ...)` unbound, against the conversation's
   own object, is what makes the test mean what it says.
2. **A flag switched off after the fact is a race with a thread.** The
   "only this turn fails" test set `assistant.fail = False` right after the
   second `_submit`, so the *failing* turn usually won the race and answered
   normally - and the first run reported the failing text **in** `order`.
   Keyed on the message text instead: `fail_on == text`.

The lesson is the one this repository keeps re-learning in a new costume: **a
harness that does not reproduce production's object graph will report a fixed
bug as unfixed, and the first reaction is to doubt the fix.** Both of these
were harness faults and neither would have been found without running the test
against the unfixed code and reading what it claimed.

## The last 17 pages: 0 of 17 rendered, then 17 of 17 (2026-10-13)

The `setup:*` wizard pages had **never once been rendered in this repository's
history**. They are the only UI surface here with no picture behind it, and this
file's standing warning is that "a page that does not render is not necessarily a
broken page" - which is right, and is also **not enough**, because the right
response to "don't believe the FAIL" is to find out why.

**Final clean run: 17 targets, `17 rendered, 0 not`, exit 0.** Measured for
genuineness afterwards by decoding alpha on every file: **17 of 17 at 100% opaque,
zero false passes.** The audit line *"never once rendered: 0 of 29"* is now
**29 of 29** for the window pages and **17 of 17** for the wizard.

**And the run that got there is worth recording, because four attempts did not.**

| attempt | what went wrong | who |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1 page, then pool exhaustion on all 16 | the `rm -f` bug, now fixed |
| 2 | 13 of 17, then exhaustion | 2 stray sweeps of my own still running |
| 3 | 2 of 8, then exhaustion | 2 stray sweeps again |
| 4 | **17 of 17** | nothing else running |

Every failure after the first was **my own harness interference**, and two of the
ways I caused it are the exact traps this file already documents:

- **Editing `render_ui_batch.sh` while a sweep was executing it.** Bash reads a
  script incrementally, so the running sweep died with
  `syntax error near unexpected token ';;'` at line 549 - eleven lines into a
  function I was editing. The file's own rule is "do not edit it while a sweep
  is executing", and it is right for the reason that is not obvious: the failure
  looks like a syntax error in the script, not like a race.
- **`pkill`/`ps|grep` self-match.** My "is anything else running?" check used
  `ps -eo args | grep -c '[r]ender_ui_batch'`, and the `[r]` trick that hides the
  pattern from `grep` does nothing when the pattern is a substring of **my own
  command line**. I read that check as "provably nothing else alive" and acted on
  it. The next command put a `kill` loop over the same pattern and **killed my own
  shell** - SIGTERM, no output. This is the trap recorded under "Kill a stale suite
  in one command and start the new one in another", reached from a different
  direction: the bracket guard protects `grep` from itself and does nothing about
  the enclosing shell.

**What the four attempts do establish is the fix.** `acquire_display`'s `rm -f` of
a live-but-slow daemon's socket was cascading one slow start into all 31 numbers;
with that removed, the same script runs all 17 to completion on a pool of 31.

**And `setup:cloud-keys` is no longer a false pass.** It measured **7.2% opaque
and 129,834 bytes** in the runs above, against 100% opaque for its siblings - the
detached-subtree capture this file already documents for editable widgets. It now
renders fully. The void-mark change is the only edit between those renders that
touches this file, so it is the likely reason, **but that mechanism is not proved
and is not claimed** - the measurement is the fact, and the attribution is not.

### The detector, now that there is a population to calibrate it against

A page sweep should print **opaque percentage** beside bytes and treat anything
below a stated floor as NOT RENDERED rather than PASS. The floor is no longer a
guess: across 17 wizard pages and 4 window pages, every genuine render is
**100%** and every false pass measured **7.2%** or **96.2% transparent**. Nothing
sits in between, and **no byte count separates them** - a false pass at 129,834
bytes outranks a real page at 25,932.

## The Languages page had a download that measured "0 MB" (2026-10-13)

The Languages wizard page is one of the seventeen this audit rendered for the
first time ever. Reading it turned up a row saying

> **ਪੰਜਾਬੀ - Punjabi** — **0 MB** - text only (no voice yet)

beside eleven rows carrying real sizes. Measured, not inferred:

| language | bytes | rendered | honest |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Tamil | 3,237,963 | 3 MB | 3.1 MiB |
| Gujarati | 1,418,394 | 1 MB | 1.4 MiB |
| **Punjabi** | **497,721** | **0 MB** | **486.1 KiB** |
| Nepali | 1,002,911 | 1 MB | 979.4 KiB |

`{n / 1e6:.0f}` rounds anything under 500,000 bytes to zero, so a real 486 KiB
download rendered as **a download of nothing** - the absence-shaped wrong answer
this file records everywhere else. It is the **same bug class already fixed in
`edit_image`** (*"`0 KB, was 0 KB` for anything under 512 bytes"*), and
`files.human_size` - which exists precisely to avoid it - was used **zero times**
in `setup_wizard.py`.

**Two copies of it, which is the part worth keeping.** There was a `_mb` helper
at `setup_wizard.py:964`, and the Languages page inlined its own
`f"{languages.install_size(code) / 1e6:.0f} MB"` beside it. One contract, two
implementations, one of which nobody was reading - the shape this file records
for `wpctl` (three copies), the finite check (four), and `capabilities._GROUPS`.
The page now goes through the helper, so a second page cannot reintroduce it.

**And the units meet in exactly one place.** `human_size` is 1024-based and `_mb`
is 1000-based; both are right in their own convention, so the small-value branch
is the only point on a row where a KiB sits next to an MB. That is stated in the
docstring rather than left as a surprise.

### The render that verified nothing, which is the part I nearly filed as verification

The first application was **overwritten by a concurrent mutation run** (pid
318684), whose `finally` restore puts the original text back over anything
written while it holds the file. I only noticed because the verification render
came back at **77,108 bytes - byte-identical to the pre-fix render**.

**A render whose size does not move is a render that proved nothing**, and it is
the same lesson as `setup:cloud-keys`' 129,834-byte false pass, reached from the
opposite direction: that one was too big, this one was unchanged. Neither is
detectable by "a file appeared", which is the whole of the sweep's PASS test.

**The fix was staged outside the tree** (`/tmp/opencode/fix_mb.py`, both anchors
asserted) precisely because `/tmp` is not something a `finally` in the repository
can restore. Applying an edit to a file another process holds open is not a
commit race; it is writing into something that is about to be overwritten.

## Every model tier stated its size twice, in two unit systems, disagreeing (2026-10-13)

The model-picker wizard page - rendered for the first time ever, like the rest of
the wizard - showed every row's size **twice**:

| row | title | subtitle |
|---|---|---|
| Very large | **4.7 GB** | **5.0 GB download** |
| Huge | **8.4 GB** | **9.0 GB download** |
| Mixture of experts | **17.3 GB** | **18.6 GB download** |

Two numbers for one quantity, side by side on the same row, both plausible, and
the row below them says "Nothing is downloaded yet". **Measured against the
source** rather than argued from the picture - `local_llm.py`'s `TIERS` carries
both a `size_bytes` and a hand-written label containing its own size:

| tier | `size_bytes` | decimal GB | GiB | label said |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Very large | 5,027,783,488 | **5.0** | 4.68 | 4.7 GB |
| Huge | 9,001,752,960 | **9.0** | 8.38 | 8.4 GB |
| Mixture of experts | 18,556,685,824 | **18.6** | 17.28 | 17.3 GB |

**The labels were GiB written with a "GB" suffix.** The comment two lines above
the last tier says *"17.3 GiB on disk"* - correct in its own unit - and the label
below it dropped the `i`. The wizard's subtitle computes from
`size_bytes / 1e9`, so every row reported the same file twice and the two figures
differed by exactly the 1.0737 factor between the units.

The first three tiers agreed only because 0.6 GB and 0.6 GiB round alike at one
decimal place, which is why this survived: **the coincidence is the only reason
three rows looked right.**

**Three numbers corrected, and the derivation is the proper fix.** The labels are
prose - *"quick on any computer, for simple requests"* is hand-written by nature
- but the size inside them is a fact `size_bytes` already states exactly, and
nothing derives one from the other. Making the parenthetical a formatted field
rather than a literal is the right shape and was **not** done here, because
`TIERS` is read positionally in more than one place and that is a wider change
than a defect fix should be here. **So this entry records the remaining work
rather than pretending the duplication is gone.**

**Note that this figure is quoted in this file in several places** - "17.3 GB",
"17.3 GiB", "18.6 GB" appear across the `local_llm` and model-tier entries - and
every one of them inherits whichever unit the writer typed. **A number copied into
prose is a number nobody re-measures**, which is the same lesson as the
`skills_total` figure this file had to correct once already.

Verified: all six labels now agree with their own `size_bytes` to one decimal
place (0 disagreements across the six), the page re-renders **87,175 -> 87,370
bytes**, and 134 passed / 1 skipped across the model-picker, model-requirements,
menu-label, ctxfit and thread suites.
## Six refusals that consumed what you asked, and one test that could not fail (2026-10-13)

The review turned into a batch, because six separate findings turned out to be
**one defect in six costumes**: the app accepted something from a person and
then threw it away, on a path where the person had no way to notice.

| what was destroyed | where | how a person hit it |
|---|---|---|
| the retry on a failed turn | `gui/widgets.py` | asking again, with no way to ask again |
| messages still queued | `app/voice.py` | Stop, with questions left unanswered on screen |
| the question | `app/brain.py` | asking while the model sleeps |
| the question | `app/brain.py` | **the first message typed on any fresh install** |
| the attachment chips | `gui/attaching.py` | attaching files, then being refused for want of a model |
| findability of a notice | `gui/widgets.py` | searching for the compaction that lost an answer |

**Two of the six are regressions this session introduced** while fixing other
things, and that is the part worth remembering:

- Marking a failure as a notice row stopped it reading as something Chronoa
  said - and **quietly removed the "Ask that again" button**, because capability
  here comes from **which builder ran**, not from what the row is about. The turn
  that most needs redoing became the one turn that cannot be redone.
- The same change stopped the error being the turn's text, and `find()` reads
  `_turns`, so an error that used to be findable stopped being findable.

### `brain.py` is the sharpest, because its own neighbouring branch gets it right

`_explain_no_model` has three branches and they treat your question three
different ways:

| branch | what happens to your text |
|---|---|
| model installed, not running | starts the service, then **re-submits the same `text`** |
| model asleep | tells you to ask again - text dropped |
| **no model at all** (every fresh install) | opens setup - text dropped |

`window._submit_input` clears the composer, the draft *and* the attachment chips
before it emits, so once a refusal returns, the question is gone from the only
place it was written. The transcript keeps the question and never the answer.

So the branch that handles "your model is merely stopped" is careful enough to
re-send your text, while the branch every new install takes throws it away -
before a 1 GB download the person may walk away from.

**Restored to the composer, not re-sent.** A download takes minutes; answering a
question typed that long ago unprompted is its own surprise. `set_input_text`
already existed as the deliberate "show this in the box" half of "send this".

### The promise I nearly shipped was half true

The first version of the message said **"your question is back in the box"** -
but `take_attachments()` clears the chips on the way out, so three attached
files were silently gone while the sentence claimed a handover. Restoring two
of three pieces of state is the failure mode, not a partial success, so
`restore_last_sent` is one door for composer, draft and chips together.

### The search index is a **dict**, and I corrected my own reason for it

I first said `_turns` is "mutated in three places". Measured: **two** - the
`del` in `truncate_from_turn` and the `= []` in `clear`. Three of the four sites
are appends or reads. I had asserted a count I had not checked, in the direction
that made me look more careful than I was.

### Three of my own witnesses could not fail, and the mutation run said so

**12 mutations, 12 caught** - but only after three attempts at the last one, and
the first version of the batch reported **14 caught** when two of them had never
executed at all:

1. **The mutation harness read `sys.argv[3]` for a path it was never given.**
   All twelve printed `20 passed` - a table of false cleans that looked perfect.
2. **The snapshot backup used `basename`.** There are **three** `voice.py` files
   (`app/`, `gui/surfaces/`, `settings_window/`) and `restore` overwrote
   `app/voice.py` with another module's body, so everything after the first
   mutation failed to import - including "unmutated".
3. **The rewind witness passed with the deletion removed, twice.** `find()`
   iterates `_turns`, so once the rewind empties the transcript there is nothing
   to match against and `find(...) == []` is true regardless of the notes. The
   sequence that bites is a **partial** rewind and then rebuilding turns into
   the space it leaves; a full rewind goes through `clear()`, which resets the
   notes anyway and masks the missing deletion.

### And the fake window's own comment predicted this

`tests/test_assistd_sayri_harvest.py` carries the line *"this comment is here so
the next method added is noticed"*, above a three-method `SimpleNamespace`. It
failed with `AttributeError` exactly as written. Its `restore_last_sent` is now
recorded and asserted, so the next method breaks the test here rather than
reading as a product defect three files away.

**Suite at the point of change: 10,825 passed, 37 failed, 70 errors across 8
chunks.** None of the failures are from this work - the 69-error chunk is live
audio in parallel shards, `model_registry.verify_digest` is the other session's,
and the models-card failure is this box having no local model.

## The sidebar dots were measured, not guessed, and the red one is honest (2026-10-13)

An earlier note in this file carried "4 of 13 coloured dots non-green (amber ×2,
red ×2, the red at bottom being **Export**, uninvestigated)" and filed nothing,
because two probes had already been shown to lie. Measured properly this time,
the number is **three**, and the cause of each is named:

| state | colour | rows |
|---|---|---|
| `status-ok` | green | Conversations, Compare, Activity, Skills, Triggers, Goals, Workbench, Diff (**8**) |
| `status-unknown` | amber | Memory, Routines (**2**) |
| `status-attention` | red | **Driving** (**1**) |
| `status-off` | grey | My files, Meetings (**2**) |

**13 dots, 8 + 2 + 1 + 2. The earlier "red ×2" was wrong and Export is not on a
dot at all** - the item below the visible sidebar is the bottom of the scroll, so
a dot inferred as "the next one down" was never measured to exist.

### And the one red dot is the panel telling the truth

`driving.py:120` records `STATUS_ATTENTION` with the word **"No display this
driver can measure"**, and the driver is `xdotool` - which is **absent from this
box**, as this file already records. So on a headless render the dot is an
accurate report, not a warning about nothing: the panel genuinely cannot place a
window here.

**This is the fourth time the health vocabulary has been right and the *reading*
of it wrong**, after `heard-sound`'s dead switch, the `0 MB` download two
entries ago, and `cloud-keys`' 129KB false pass. A red mark in a screenshot is a
claim about colour until something asks what produced it.

### The instrument that finally worked, because the first three did not

The dots are at **x = 36..40** - which is inside the same column as the row
**icons** (x = 32..44). The first probe scanned x = 55..85, found exactly one
chromatic pixel cluster, and reported it as *the entire status column*; it was
the **Routines icon's orange badge**. The second lumped icons and dots together
and concluded "coloured pixels live at 32..44", which is true and says nothing
about which is which. The third guessed y-coordinates from looking at a picture
and hit empty rows three times.

What worked was **chroma clustering over the correct column** - and the only
reason the column was found is that the one dot the wrong probe *did* find was
magnified, cropped and looked at rather than reported. **A magnified crop is a
different instrument from a coordinate scan**, and here it was the one that said
the instrument was aimed at the wrong pixels.

### The "colour-only indicator" hypothesis was wrong, and checking cost one grep

Colour alone excludes colourblind users, so a sidebar whose only state signal is
a 10px dot looked like a defect. `sidebar.py:387` sets
`dot.set_tooltip_text(f"{title}: {STATUS_WORDS[status]}")` - so the state is
named in words on hover, and the dot is a summary of a labelled indicator rather
than the indicator. The grep for it was one line; **the defect was in the
hypothesis, which is what the measurement is for.**

## The Export panel said "Needs attention" about a machine that had said nothing yet (2026-10-13)

The 33 panel renders had not been looked at. `voice`, `skills` and `machine` are
clean; `export` was not, and the defect is one this file has already fixed **in
the sibling panel** earlier today.

> 🔴 **Needs attention**
> Nothing to export - there is no open conversation yet - the first thing you say
> becomes one

A fresh install, working perfectly, carrying a red dot and the app's one warning
colour. It is the **absence-shaped wrong answer**, and it is the identical defect
`compare` held for its empty store — where this file already records that the
fix was `STATUS_OK` with *"Nothing to compare yet"*. **`compare.py` was corrected
and `export.py` was its unfixed twin**, which is the "one fix, one place" shape
this file records for `wpctl` (three copies), the finite check (four) and
`capabilities._GROUPS`.

### The fix could not be a blanket `STATUS_OK`, and that is the measurement

`_open_conversation` returns a `reason` from **four** causes, and the caller
collapsed all four into red:

| line | reason | a fault? |
|---|---|---|
| 491 | the store could not be opened | **yes** |
| 494 | `NO_CONVERSATION_REASON` — nothing said yet | no |
| 498 | the open conversation could not be read | **yes** |
| 500 | the open conversation has no messages yet | no |

Blanket-`OK` would **delete a red alarm about a real failure** — the over-fix
this file records for the `get_children` guard, where "the call must be absent"
would have been satisfied by deleting the working `hasattr`.

So `_open_conversation` now returns a **fourth element**, `could_not_read`, and
the row branches on it. **Carried as a flag rather than inferred from the
reason's text**, because deciding "is this a fault?" by matching an error's
wording is how `manage_triggers` once armed every malformed source — it matched
the openings of its readers' refusal sentences.

### Measured both ways, in pixels and in the widget

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| status row word | **Needs attention** | **Ready** |
| detail | "Nothing to export - …" | "Nothing to export yet - …" |
| the dot's own colour | **`(239, 68, 68)`** = `#ef4444`, the literal in `.status-attention` | **`(34, 181, 88)`** = `rgba(34,197,94,0.9)` from `.status-ok` |
| render | 185,548 B, sha `f6b2f4686cc2` | 185,303 B, sha `b51438252d01` |

The colour is the app's own CSS constant read back out of the rendered pixels,
so "the dot is green" is not a description of a picture — it is the hex the
stylesheet declares.

**Four tests, both directions, and the shipped defect restored fails 4 of 4.**
The half that must survive is asserted first: a store that cannot be opened is
still `STATUS_ATTENTION`, and the panel says *"Could not read the conversation
store"* rather than *"Nothing to export yet"*. **A fix that cannot be over-applied
is not a fix yet**, and this one could have been. 52 passed / 1 skipped in the
file.

**And one of my own four was a check that could not fail, in a new costume.** It
asserted `count("True") == 2` in the helper's source — *counting* rather than
*measuring*, the same mistake as every length-assertion this file has retracted.
Replaced with the method driven directly (it touches no `self`), which is what
caught that `_open_conversation`'s two `True`s and two `False`s are a fact about
what it **decides**, not about how many times a word appears.

### The sentence is still said three times, and that is left alone

The reason appears in the banner, in the status row's detail, and in the section
description beneath it. **That is real and it was measured, and it is not fixed
here** — the repetition predates this defect, the status row's detail is where
the *cause* belongs rather than under the section heading, and removing one of
the three is an editorial judgement about which two carry information. Recorded
rather than tidied, because the one thing that was wrong here was a **red dot on
a working machine**, and that is fixed and pinned.
## A draft belongs to the conversation it was written for, and one test file was polluting every other (2026-10-13)

The last item the UI review found, and the one that had been sitting in plain
sight behind a fix.

`show_conversation()` redraws the transcript and **never touched the composer**.
So a half-typed question followed the person: open another conversation and the
box still held what you were writing to the previous one, and Enter put it into
the new one - silently, because the transcript then shows your question in a
conversation it has nothing to do with.

**`Ctrl+N` was already fixed for exactly this.** `_reset_conversation` clears the
composer and carries a comment describing the bug in full - *"the next Enter sent
a question about the previous conversation into the new one, and nothing on
screen said so"*. So the hole was only in **switching**, and the existing fix
**hid the shape of it**: the obvious conclusion from `clear_input()` on Ctrl+N is
"the composer is handled", and it is handled on exactly one of the two paths.

`composer_draft` already took an optional `path` on every function. Per-
conversation drafts were supported at the module level the whole time; the
window simply never passed one.

### Text and files move together, or not at all

A draft is a sentence *and* the attachments that sentence refers to. Restoring
the words and leaving the chip bar empty shows somebody reading "check these
three files" above nothing - the partial restore this module's own docstring
calls worse than none. They go in **one** record, because one atomic replace is
what keeps them from arriving out of step.

The key is sanitised because it arrives from a session reference, and a
reference containing `../` would write outside the directory whose `0o700` and
`0o600` are load-bearing - a file holding what somebody was typing, written
somewhere unprotected.

### Switching is moved, not destroyed - and always empties first

Going back finds what you left, which is what `Ctrl+N` used to throw away. And
`set_conversation` clears the composer **before** restoring, because
`restore_draft` returns early when there is no draft: without that line a
conversation with nothing typed opened showing the previous one's words -
**the misfire reintroduced one line after being fixed**, and the test written
for it caught it on the first run.

### Two more witnesses that could not fail

| witness | why it passed on broken code |
|---|---|
| `_store` wrapped `draft_path` in a lambda that re-rooted its result | **the key sanitisation never ran**, so the escape test passed with `safe = str(key)` in place - a stub answering the question it was meant to check |
| `assert _draft_timeout is None` after a switch | `_flush_draft` *also* sets it to `None`, so the attribute says "nothing pending" whether or not the timer was unregistered. `GLib.MainContext.find_source_by_id` is the only thing that tells those apart, and measured: non-None before `source_remove`, None after |

And two fixtures of mine that did not reproduce production, in the two costumes
this repo keeps finding: one typed a draft **before** naming the conversation,
which production never does; the other typed *"belongs to beta"* while still in
alpha and complained that alpha kept it - **which is the draft module working
correctly.**

### `test_composer_draft.py` was leaking a stub into the whole session

`_point_store_at` assigns `composer_draft.draft_path = lambda key=None: target`
**directly, not through `monkeypatch`, and never restores it** - and that lambda
ignores its key. Run alongside the new file, five tests failed with *"both
conversations resolve to the same draft file"*, which had nothing to do with
per-conversation drafts and everything to do with a stub installed three files
earlier. Now restored by an autouse fixture.

The same defect `run_suite_in_chunks.sh` records as *"every chunk shared one
`XDG_STATE_HOME`"*, reached through a module attribute instead of a directory: **a
test that changes global state and does not give it back.**

### 9 mutations, 9 caught, after fixing both vacuous witnesses

| mutation | |
|---|---|
| switching does not empty the composer | 3 failed |
| the armed save survives the switch | 1 failed |
| every key shares one file | 4 failed |
| the key is not sanitised | 1 failed |
| the words are not cleared on a switch | 2 failed |
| the files are not restored with the words | 1 failed |
| empty text keeps its files | 1 failed |

### The other session's mutation runs restore the tree from git

Twice now, a `mutate.py` run wiped **uncommitted** work in `conversation.py` and
`application.py` while my other files survived - so the damage is partial and
looks like a mystery rather than a restore. The lesson is not to leave work
uncommitted across a window in which another session is running: this batch was
committed within seconds of the tests passing for exactly that reason.

## Every other "absence reported as a fault" was measured, and all of them are correct (2026-10-13)

`export` was not a one-off: it is a shape this file has now corrected four times
(the `heard-sound` dead switch, the Compare panel's empty store, the `0 MB`
download, and this). So rather than look at 29 more renders for the same
symptom, the whole population was swept: **every `STATUS_ATTENTION` in
`gui/surfaces/`**, each classified by what it is actually attached to.

**One live instance. Five cleared, and the clearances are the useful half** -
each is a place a reader would otherwise "fix", and two of them are the
reference implementation of the rule `export` broke.

| panel | its red row | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| `inventory` | "N of M functions absent" | **branch unreachable.** `organism.INVENTORY` is **17 built, 14 partial, 0 absent** - so `counts[ABSENT] == 0` always and the first branch always fires. **"Fixing" this would have been editing a guard no organ reaches**, which is the `defensible redundancy` outcome, not a defect. |
| `calendar` | "No calendar backend" | **correct, and it is the reference.** `_permitted()` is consulted at **line 472, before** the no-backend branch, so consent-off never reaches red. Consent-off renders `STATUS_OFF` **"Calendar is not granted"** (grey "Turned off") and an empty range renders `STATUS_OK` "No events in range". **The vocabulary expresses the distinction; one sibling already does exactly what `export` should have.** |
| `desktop` | "The desktop search provider is not installed" | **defensible, and the measurement is what says so.** `PKGBUILD:273` installs `shani-chronoa-search` with `install -Dm755` unconditionally and line 304 its D-Bus service - **no optdepend gates it**. So on an installed system its absence *is* a broken install, which is what attention is for. |
| `skills`, `workbench` | "No skills loaded" | **correct.** The detail is *"The registry returned nothing"*, and the render measured **256 skills** - so this fires only on a registry that has genuinely failed. **A registry that returned nothing on a healthy machine is a fault**, which is the opposite of export's case. |
| `model`, `models` | "No model is chosen" | **defensible.** No model means the assistant cannot answer, and this file already records `set_can_answer()` overriding the idle "Ready" for exactly that reason. |
| `voice` | "No voice engine is available" | **defensible.** `espeak-ng` is a hard `depends`, so no engine at all means a broken install rather than a missing one. |

**The two that would have been most tempting to "fix" are `inventory` (dead
branch) and `desktop` (looks like a missing optional package, is a shipped
binary).** Both would have been confident wrong answers with a green suite and a
plausible commit message, and neither was distinguishable from `export` by
reading the status call - only by counting the organs and reading the PKGBUILD.

**And `calendar` is why the export fix is not a judgement call.** It is the same
vocabulary, the same `StatusRecorder`, one directory away, doing it correctly -
which is the strongest available evidence that "nothing to export yet" belongs at
`STATUS_OK` and was an oversight rather than a deliberate reading.
## The main UI had never been rendered above 460px, and the harness said nothing (2026-10-13)

The rendering pass that had been blocked all session finally ran, and the first
thing it produced was a measurement about the **harness**, not the product.

### `CHRONOA_FORCE_SIZE=1` and how to use it

Rendering works from a clean tree with:

    env -u DISPLAY -u WAYLAND_DISPLAY bash tools/render_ui_batch.sh <out> 1024 700 main

**`DISPLAY` must be unset.** The batch driver says so in its own comment and it
is exactly why every direct invocation failed with `GDK_IS_DISPLAY (display)
failed` and `Gtk couldn't be initialized`: this machine has a live X session
(`DISPLAY=:0`, `WAYLAND_DISPLAY=wayland-0`) and **a live X display wins over
`GDK_BACKEND=broadway`**, so the renderer silently rendered onto nothing. That
was the whole of the "broadway doesn't work here" mystery.

`broadwayd :N` listens on socket **N+1**, so `BROADWAY_DISPLAY` is the *socket*
number, not the one passed to the daemon. There is no `--size` option.

### Every picture of the main window was 460x640, whatever was asked for

`render_ui.py` honours a window's own default size, and says why: *"a window that
sized itself keeps its own size"* - so Quick Ask's `set_default_size(460, -1)`
popup is not stretched into a full screen with 730px of nothing under it. That
reasoning is sound.

**But `ChronoaWindow` declares `set_default_size(460, 640)`** in `_setup_window`
- correctly, the app really does open at 460x640 - so the same rule clamped
*every* capture of the main window, and **there was no way to ask for anything
else**. Measured, with the size traced from inside `_render`:

    argv=['render_ui.py', 'main', '/tmp/chronoa-t/main.png', '1024', '700']
    WIDTH=460 HEIGHT=640   alloc=460x640   default=(width=460, height=640)

`main` at 1280x860 and at 1000x700 produced **byte-identical 460x640 PNGs**.

That is not cosmetic. At 460 the sidebar, the rail and the two-column transcript
are all collapsed by the app's own breakpoints, so **every layout that only
exists when the window is wide had no picture at all** - the sidebar open, the
rail with its eight sections, the header's full title instead of "Shani...".
The whole point of looking is to see those, and the default made them
unreachable while still reporting `PASS` and a plausible byte count.

**`CHRONOA_FORCE_SIZE=1` overrides it.** Default behaviour is unchanged, so the
Quick Ask reasoning still stands; what was missing was a way to ask for the other
one. With it, `main` renders at **1024x700, 86,956 bytes** - nearly double, and a
different window.

### What the wide render actually shows

- **The sidebar, the rail, and the full header title "Shani Chronoa"** all exist
  and look right. Nothing broken was found in them.
- **The permission chips are two different chips, not one regressed one.**
  `"No questions"` is the *posture* (`window.py:344`) and `"Nothing leaves"` is
  the *privacy* one (`window.py:498`); the strip shows the posture currently set,
  which is `"Ask first"`. I had written down that the render showed a regression
  and it was wrong - worth recording, because it is the second time this session
  that reading carefully beat looking carefully.
- **The organ strip's labels still read as one run-on string** at 1024:
  *"listening looking speaking network sensing remembering acting thinking"*.
  That is the **same symptom** `organs.py`'s 6px `set_column_spacing` was
  introduced to cure, and
  `test_now_rail.py::test_the_organ_lights_are_separated_by_a_gap` pins the
  number. A 6px gap between two lowercase words reads as a space, not a
  boundary. **Not changed here**: it is a value a test pins, a CSS half was
  previously moved around to avoid, and one render is not a basis for tuning it.
  It needs an A/B at two or three widths and the test updated deliberately.

### The override blanked the help window, and looking is how I found out

`CHRONOA_FORCE_SIZE` as first written forced **every** window. Applied to `help`
- a modal dialog - it rendered **a blank white page**:

| | size | bytes |
|---|---|---|
| without the override | 638x620 | **110,103** |
| with the override | 1024x700 | **25,346** |

Both reported `PASS`. That is precisely *"a broken picture from a successful
render, which is the worst of both"* - the failure this module's docstring says
it exists to prevent - and **I introduced it ten minutes earlier**.

The fix is not a special case but the rule the block was already expressing:
**a modal dialog's size is its design**, the same reason Quick Ask is a 460x170
popup. So modals are excluded, and `help` renders at its own 638x620 with its
content intact.

**The lesson is about method, not about GTK.** Every check I had run on that
change was a byte count and an exit status, and all of them were satisfied by a
picture of a white rectangle. Nothing short of looking at the image would have
caught it, and the render batch reported `PASS` for both.

## Looking at intermediate widths: the sidebar hyphenates "Meetings" (2026-10-13)

With the harness able to render above 460 for the first time, the next useful
thing was the width *between* the two layouts the app collapses at.

Rendered `state:composer-question` at **760x700** (the target is a full window,
not a bare widget):

- 1024 wide: sidebar fine, title "Shani Chronoa", rail present.
- **760 wide: the sidebar breaks single-word titles mid-word, with a hyphen.**

      Meetin-
      gs

`sidebar.py:230` builds every row as `Adw.ActionRow(title=title)` and there is
**no `set_ellipsize` anywhere in the file** (measured: zero occurrences).
libadwaita wraps a title that does not fit, and Pango breaks a word with a
hyphen when it cannot break at a space - so "My files" wraps at the space and
looks fine, while **"Meetings" does not fit and comes out as two lines**. One
word, one panel, and it is the only row that breaks.

**Why it survived**: every render in this repo's history was 460 wide or the
window's own 460, and at 460 the sidebar is **collapsed** - so the rows whose
titles are long enough to break were never on screen in a picture. The defect
was not invisible; it was *unreachable by the only instrument available*.

**Not fixed here**, deliberately. The fix is small and located -
`row.set_title_widget(Gtk.Label(label=title, ellipsize=Pango.EllipsizeMode.END,
xalign=0))` in place of the title string - but it needs its own regression test
at a width that actually breaks it, and a mutation run, and this session ended
before I could do either properly. A one-line visual change with no witness is
exactly the thing this file keeps warning about.

**Also recorded, from the same render**: `state:composer-question` is
indistinguishable from `state:composer-empty` - no question, no prompt, just the
empty state. Either the builder does not put a pending question on screen or the
target is misnamed, and **no render target exists for a permission prompt at
all** (`--list states` shows only `strip-*`, `composer-*` and `organ-*`). So the
one moment where the app asks a person to trust it with an action has never had a
picture, which is a gap in the harness rather than in the product.

## Two panels drew a 55px slice of an icon instead of the sentence under it (2026-10-13)

Found by rendering `panel:triggers` and reading it. Between the consent banner
and the "Arm a rule" form there was a lone grey crescent:

> a clipped arc, flat bottom edge, nothing else on the page

No "**No trigger rules armed**" - on a panel whose entire content is that
sentence. **Reproducible, not a sweep artefact**: two independent renders put
**1859 pixels** of the icon's own grey `(156,156,156)` at *identical*
coordinates.

### The cause is a measurement, and it is one number

`Adw.StatusPage` declares a **minimum height of 301px** and a minimum width of
152px, *whatever height it is offered*:

| offered | its minimum |
|---:|---:|
| 900 | **301** |
| 200 | **301** |
| 50 | **301** |
| 20 | **301** |

The icon is drawn **centred** in the 301px it insists on, so a container that
can give it a fraction shows **a band across the middle** of the icon - which is
why it reads as a stray shape rather than as a truncated one.

**`goals` is the control and it renders perfectly**: full icon, title,
description, button - because it gives its `StatusPage` the whole page. A
page-level widget mounted **inline**, in a scrolled content box beside other
content, is the wrong widget for the space it is given.

| panel | what was on screen instead of the sentence |
|---|---|
| `triggers` | the crescent, and **no title and no description** |
| `memory` | a clipped prohibition icon, and no title - the title also ran off as *"...not available to t"* |

`common.empty_state()` takes **`inline=True`**, which builds the squeezable box
the module already had for the no-Adw case rather than a `StatusPage`. Both
measured panels pass it. **`goals` does not, and renders byte-identically**
(sha `fd89a459256e`, unchanged) - the control that says the fix is a placement
switch and not "stop using StatusPage".

### Two pre-existing gaps the fix exposed, both caught by the layout contract

1. **The box's heading was never wrapped** - only its description was. Invisible
   while the branch was reached only when Adw was unavailable, because
   `Adw.StatusPage` wraps its own title. `test_long_labels_wrap_or_ellipsise
   [memory]` went red the moment a panel used it.
2. **`memory` had no `Gtk.ScrolledWindow` of its own** - it was passing
   `test_every_surface_can_scroll` only because the `Adw.StatusPage` it no
   longer uses **contains one internally**.

Both are the same shape as each other and of the export defect: **a guard that
was passing because of a widget it no longer used.**

### 3 mutations, 3 caught, and the control is a test not a comment

`inline` ignored (the shipped behaviour) -> **2 failed**; the heading unwrapped
-> **1**; the scroller removed -> **3**. Every one restores the file
byte-identical.

The control is `TestThePageEmptyStateIsUnchanged`: it asserts the page variant
is **still** an `Adw.StatusPage` and still carries its child. **A guard that only
checked the inline variant would be satisfied by a helper that stopped building
a StatusPage at all** - which would silently change the 34 other call sites.

**And `test_the_measured_floor_is_still_the_floor` re-derives the 301** rather
than trusting the constant, so a libadwaita upgrade is visible instead of
silently invalidating the bound the other tests are written against.

### Five detectors that measured nothing, which is the other half of this

Finding the second panel meant recognising the signature across 33 renders, and
**five detectors in a row reported a clean tree while looking straight at it**:

| attempt | why it reported 0 |
|---|---|
| "most common colour in the row" | the **background** always wins, and my `>120` filter then excluded it - so on exactly the icon's rows the background was the answer |
| exact colour equality across rows | the icon is **antialiased**; its colour moves 1-2 per row, so every run broke |
| bucket the colour, then compare | fixed that, and still missed it: **193px was a bounding box, not a per-row run** |
| 90px per-row threshold | the crescent's rows are ~34px; `memory`'s are ~157px, so the threshold found one and not the other |
| 40px threshold, restructured | a closure bug in my own `close()` helper |

**A scan that cannot find the thing you are looking at reports the same clean
result as one that works.** What finally worked was the rule "the longest run
whose colour differs from the background" - and what found `memory` was not the
detector at all but **cropping the region and looking**, after the detector had
already pointed at it once.

## The organ gap test protects a value that still produces the symptom it names (2026-10-13)

The last item from the render pass, and the honest answer is about the **witness**,
not the spacing.

Renders at **760** and **1024** - both widths the harness could only reach once
`CHRONOA_FORCE_SIZE` existed - both show the eight organ labels reading as one
string:

    listening looking speaking network sensing remembering acting thinking

That is **exactly the symptom** `set_column_spacing(6)` was introduced to cure.
`organs.py` records the whole story: zeroing the `flowboxchild` padding recovered
~230px of width "and left nothing between the lights, so the eight labels
rendered as ... one run-on string, not eight named lights". Six pixels is the fix
for that.

**And 6px does not fix it.** A six-pixel gap between two lowercase words reads as
a space, not a boundary. Two renders at two widths say so.

**The test does not catch this, and cannot:**

    assert strip.get_column_spacing() >= 4

A floor of 4 is satisfied by the shipped 6, so the witness passes **with the
symmetric symptom fully present**. It was written to protect the property its
docstring names - "the strip's width test passes on a row nobody can read" - and
the value it chose does not deliver it. That is the same shape as the seven
vacuous witnesses elsewhere this session, arrived at from the other direction:
a test that is *not* vacuous, passes truthfully, and still does not protect the
thing.

**Not changed**, and the reason is the measurement I could not finish. The
spacing also governs whether the strip wraps to two rows, which is a documented
prior bug: homogeneous cells wrapped "even at 1280px (measured) because six wide
cells plus two is a line break, not because the words needed it". Widening the
gap costs `7 x delta` pixels across the strip, and I could not measure the
strip's natural width per spacing in the time left - the broadway daemon died
mid-measurement and GTK4 widgets cannot be measured without a display.

So the change needs, in this order:

1. the strip's natural width at spacings 6 / 12 / 18, measured;
2. the column width available to it at 760 and at 1024, from a render;
3. the smallest spacing at which the labels read as eight things;
4. the test's floor raised to **that** number, so the witness protects the
   property it names.

Changing the constant first and rendering afterwards would be the same mistake as
the one this session already made once - forcing a render size and checking byte
counts, which produced a picture of a white rectangle and passed every check.


## The constrained-decoding caution now has two independent sources, and the tool still truncates abstracts (2026-12)

Ran the sweep through the shipped `web_search(source="arxiv")` - the entry point
built for exactly this - rather than a hand-rolled script, which is the point of
having built it. Six queries over the open question **"why do three fine-tunes
move a tool-calling model from 4/5 to 0/3 at any scale?"**, and the answer is not
in the LoRA literature; it is in the constrained-decoding line.

**The one paper worth naming.** *From Hallucination to Structure Snowballing: The
Alignment Tax of Constrained Decoding in LLM Reflection* (arXiv:**2604.06066**,
cs.CL, Hongxu Zhou, 2026). "Alignment tax" is the name for a cost this repository
had as a **single** source: `AGENTS.md` already recorded AdapTrack
(arXiv:2510.17376) quoting "constrained decoding distorts the model's output
intent... up to 7.84% on HumanEval, 6.42% on MBPP, 38.93% on API completion".
2604.06066 is a **second, unrelated method reaching the same place from a
different direction** - and two independent sources is what turns a caution into
a measured position rather than one paper's result.

**So the recommendation is unchanged and better supported.** The three-arm
experiment the file already prescribes - base; grammar-constrained; and
**format-request-without-enforcement** as the control - is the right shape for a
second reason: without the third arm a gain is attributable to the grammar when
arXiv:2607.18476 says the register alone does the work. That arm is the whole
experiment, and it is still not run.

**What I verified and what I did not, stated rather than implied.** Verified:
the titles, authors, years, categories and URLs of six papers, read out of the
real feed. **Not verified: any abstract, any number, any result.** `_parse_arxiv`
puts the bibliographic facts first and the abstract is a **truncated tail** - a
deliberate design decision in the module, not a defect - so everything above the
title line in that paper's entry is what the tool exposes and everything below it
I have not read. Citing a figure from 2604.06066 would be citing a title.

**Two more from the same sweep, both named and neither read:**
*Rethinking Inter-LoRA Orthogonality in Adapter Merging* (arxiv 2510.03262v2) -
already cited for the chimera retraction, so that claim now stands on the paper
rather than on a summary - and *Crowded in B-Space* (2604.16826), the one the
111x delta-norm spread was measured against. Both were found by the shipped tool
in about a second, which is the return on having built it.

### Unresolved: the question row still does not appear in the capture

Recorded so it is not mistaken for fixed. `composer-question` now drives a real
API - `_clear_question_widgets()`, a wrapped label appended to `_question_row`,
then `set_visible(True)` - rather than calling an attribute that does not exist

not on screen.**

Two paths put a question on screen and the render follows only one:

- `gui/asking.py:55-64` - the **interactive** one: the question, a row of option
  buttons, a dimmed hint, then `set_visible(True)`.
- `gui/questions.py:128-137` - the **`ask_user` skill** one: a bare label.

The render now mirrors the second. Whether the row is being clipped, is placed

the row is appended to it, so on paper it should appear between the transcript

**What is worth knowing: the trust moment has no picture at all.** No target
