## "Conversation checkpoints" was red on a machine where nothing had been said (2026-10-13)

The `export` fix two entries above was the fourth correction of this shape, and
the first entry asked for the whole population to be swept rather than the other
29 renders looked at. The sweep cleared every other `STATUS_ATTENTION`. **The
next instance was in a panel the sweep could not see**, because it is the
Diagnostics panel's **own three-word vocabulary** - `working` / `not working` /
`could not determine` - rather than `common.STATUS_*`. Six panels were cleared;
the seventh has its own words and was not in the scan.

**Its docstring stated the rule it broke.** `diagnostics._checkpoint_count`:

> A missing session directory is the normal "nothing done yet" state, **not a
> fault**, so that reports nothing rather than a red dot.

and **both** branches below it returned `STATUS_NOT_WORKING` - including the
`not root.exists()` branch, which is the exact case the sentence names. A panel
section above it says the same thing in prose: *"A missing session dir is not an
error - it means no conversations have been started yet."* So the panel
contradicted itself twice, in one file, in the same words.

**Zero checkpoints is two facts, and the code treated it as one.**

| state | was | now | why |
|---|---|---|---|
| store never created | red | **green** | nothing to rewind |
| store empty | red | **green** | nothing to rewind |
| **conversation saved, no checkpoint** | red | **red** | rewinding it would silently do nothing |
| store unreadable | *green, counting zero* | **"could not determine"** | it could not find out |
| checkpoints present | green | green | unchanged |

The third row is the one a blanket fix would have deleted, and it is why the
sentence above is a **two-state** change rather than a colour change: the
remedies are opposite. The fourth was a **confident wrong answer** the old code
could not produce, because it never asked.

### The docstring was also wrong about which function knows how to count

> `conversation_store.list_checkpoints` is the one place that knows how to
> enumerate them; a probe should use it rather than reimplementing the glob

`list_checkpoints(root, sid)` is **per-session** - it needs the conversation id,
which the probe did not have, which is *why* the glob was there. So the probe
now asks `list_sessions` for the ids and `list_checkpoints` for each one's count,
and the docstring's claim becomes true rather than aspirational.

**And the probe no longer creates the store it asks about.** `list_sessions` goes
through `index()`, which makes the directory; `root.exists()` is checked first, so
a read-only diagnostic is not the thing that brings an unused store into
existence. Measured: the directory is still absent after the probe asks about it.

### The old fixture described a state the store cannot produce

The test wrote `session1.ckpt.1.jsonl` and `session2.ckpt.2.jsonl` into a
directory and asserted `"in 1 conversation(s)"` - **one**, while writing two
files. It passed only because the old glob counted *files* and called that
"conversations". `list_sessions` reads the **index**, so a directory of
checkpoint files with no index holds no conversations at all: the fixture could
never have reached the assertion it was checking. Fixtures now go through
`new_session` / `append` / `checkpoint`, and **two of the old assertions were
counting the wrong thing** - conversations where the probe counts files.

That is why the mutation run found two survivors on the first pass, and both
were the fixture's shape rather than a missing check: `sessions[:1]` (only the
first conversation counted) and `total += 1` (files counted as conversations)
left **38 green**, because every other case in the file builds one conversation.
Two tests now carry two.

### 7 mutations, 7 caught, 0 survivors

The shipped defect restored in either empty branch, the **over-fix** (a saved
conversation without a checkpoint reported as fine), an unreadable store read as
a clean zero, the directory guard removed, and both counting mutations. Run on a
**snapshot** at `/tmp/opencode/snap-diag`, never the shared tree, and the source
restored byte-identical afterwards.

**Two of my harness faults, and the first produced six false cleans.** Forcing
`GDK_BACKEND=broadway` with no `BROADWAY_DISPLAY` segfaulted before any summary,
and the harness counted `exit != 0` as **caught** - a table of six passes that
measured nothing. The second was `env -i`, which strips `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` and
`DISPLAY` and segfaults at GTK widget construction. Both are this file's own
rule arriving from a new direction: **a run with no summary is `UNMEASURABLE`,
never "caught"**, which is what `MutationDidNotParse` exists to say in
`tools/mutate.py`.

**And I measured my own fix with the wrong instrument first.** `grep "nothing to
rewind yet"` returned **0** in a file that demonstrably contained the fix,
because the sentence is split across two source lines. The same substring check
then reported the snapshot as unfixed and I nearly re-copied the tree. It is the
`skills_total` / `42/87/70` / "105 characters" mistake: **a number measured with
a pattern, then acted on.**

### Measured, not eyeballed

`panel:diagnostics` re-rendered after the fix, **205,661 B, 100% opaque** (so a
real render, not the detached-subtree false pass). Chromatic text by row, the
content column only:

| row | pixels |
|---|---|
| Local model server - genuinely broken | **6,148 red** |
| Speech in - genuinely broken | (above) |
| Speech out (espeak-ng) | green |
| **Conversation checkpoints** | **green, 0 red** |
| Microphone, Audio path | green |

The instrument is the reason the zero means something: it found red in two rows
and green in four, and **the two rows that should be red still are** - this is
not "everything turned green".

### The repetition is left in, and named

The reason now appears in the row's detail **and** in the section's prose above
it, as it did before. That is the same judgement recorded on `export`: the cause
belongs in the row, the section explains the group, and which two of the three
say it best is editorial. What was wrong here was **a red dot on a working
machine**, and that is fixed and pinned.

## The model servers were three red rows on every default install (2026-10-13)

The checkpoint entry above asked for the whole population swept rather than the
other 29 renders looked at, and the next instance was in this panel's **second**
vocabulary: `diagnostics` does not use `common.STATUS_*`, it has its own three
words. A scan of `STATUS_ATTENTION` cannot see it, which is why six panels were
cleared and this one was not looked at.

`_model_server` answers for Eyes, Imagine and Memory - the wizard's **opt-in
extras** - and it distinguished "answering" from "not answering" with no third
state for "never set up". So a machine that had installed nothing optional
carried **three red rows** in the panel whose job is to say what is broken.

**Its own docstring already had the missing case, and its own prose said it twice:**

> a server with no env file was never configured, and that is a different answer
> from one that is configured and not answering.

> The loopback servers setup starts. **Each may be asleep, which is a normal
> state for all three.**

`read_env` already returned `("", ())` for a server setup never wrote, and the
function already branched on it - to build the `setup` sentence - and then fell
through to red anyway. The code had the fact and answered the wrong question with
it.

### Two states, and the remedy is the point

| env file | answering | answer |
|---|---|---|
| present | yes | working |
| **present** | no | **not working** - somebody wanted this server |
| **absent** | no | **working** - an extra nobody installed |

`STATUS_UNKNOWN` was the tempting middle and it is a lie: this *determined* the
answer, it did not fail to. And a green row that says "nothing is wrong" without
naming a door is a dead end the person has to find elsewhere - the row names
setup's Optional extras page.

**The middle row is the one a blanket fix deletes**, so it has its own test
beside the fix's. This file records three fixes in this panel that could be
over-applied and one that was.

### 7 mutations, 7 caught - 5 by the runner, 2 verified by hand

| mutation | |
|---|---|
| the never-configured branch gone (**the shipped defect**) | 3 failed |
| **every non-answering server is green (the over-fix)** | 3 failed |
| an unconfigured extra reports "could not determine" | 1 failed |
| the row stops saying the absence is not a fault | 1 failed |
| the row stops naming the page that installs it | 1 failed |
| the remedy sentence is cut at the fault | 1 failed |
| the imagine row reports the vision server | 1 failed |

**The runner reported the first two as `UNMEASURABLE`, and they are not.** It
printed `1 error in 0.52s` for both while the other five measured normally, and
by hand - twice, including through the runner's own `_test_env()` scratch dirs -
both produce **3 failed, 43 passed**. So the two are caught and the *harness* is
what could not measure them, which is the direction this file cares about: a run
that could not measure is reported unmeasurable rather than as a survivor, and
the honest report is that five were measured by the tool and two by a person.

**And the survivor that was real: my own witness.** The Imagine-row mutation
survived twice. The test called `_model_server(instance)` directly, so rewiring
`_SECTIONS` left every direct call unchanged - the probe still describes whatever
instance it is handed. **A test that reaches past the table to the function
behind it is testing the function, not the panel**, which is the same rule as
"patch a name where it is read, not where it is re-exported" and this file's own
`goals.remove` regression. It now walks the section's rows, which is what the
panel renders, and the control is per-row: each row must name **its own** server
and **no other**, so a row naming no server at all or all three fails too.

### The prose check was the wrong instrument twice

The first version read `inspect.getsource` and asserted a substring. It failed on
the sentence that was sitting right there, because the description is written as
two adjacent string literals and the join leaves the quote between them:

    "...which is a "  "normal state for all three."
                      ^^ the `"` `"` the pattern walks into

Two wrong instruments in one test: a **source-text read for a claim about what a
person sees**, and a pattern over text a line break rewrites. `_SECTIONS` holds
the rendered string, so the claim is asked of the thing it is about - the second
time this session a pattern read as an absence, after
`grep "nothing to rewind yet"` on the checkpoint entry.

### The Model servers section cannot be photographed, which is now the third such gap

The fix above is verified by tests and mutations; **it is not verified by a
picture**, and the reason is worth writing down rather than leaving the commit
claiming more than it shows.

`_SECTIONS` has six sections in this order, and the third is the one under test:

| # | section | rows |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | The brain and speech | 3 |
| 1 | Conversations and checkpoints | 1 |
| 2 | Microphone and audio | 3 |
| 3 | Screen and desktop | 4 |
| 4 | Optional extras | 8 |
| **5** | **Model servers** | **3** |

`panel:diagnostics` rendered at **900, 1500 and 2600** pixels tall. Every one
stops at **section 2** - the last visible heading is *Microphone and audio*, with
empty space below it - so sections 3, 4 and 5 are never in a capture at any
height, and the red-pixel scan finds nothing there **because nothing is drawn**,
not because the rows are green.

That is the third time in this pass that a surface has no picture behind it, and
it is the same shape as the two already recorded: **the permission prompt has no
render target at all**, and the organ-strip gap needs a measurement nobody can
take. The generalisation is that this project's instruments reach the **top** of a
panel reliably and the bottom never; every defect found in this pass was in the
part an instrument could reach, which is exactly what the permission-prompt entry
warned about and did not act on.

**What would close it**, in order:

1. a render target that scrolls the panel's own scroller to a named section, or
   a `section:<name>` target that builds only that section - the surface already
   has `panel:` and `page:`, so a third addressing form is the gap;
2. **and then** a check on every section that `common` marks scrollable, so
   "the bottom of this panel has never been looked at" cannot recur silently -
   the same population sweep the checkpoint entry asked for, applied to
   *position* rather than to status vocabulary.

Until (1) exists, **the honest claim for this commit is "verified by 46 tests and
7 mutations, not by a render"**, and the red-pixel count on this panel means
nothing below the fold.

## The Diagnostics panel had its own vocabulary, and the absence sweep could not see it (2026-10-13)

The entry above swept **every `STATUS_ATTENTION` in `gui/surfaces/`** and cleared
five panels. That sweep was **scoped to `common.STATUS_*`** - and
`diagnostics.py` does not use them. It has its own closed three-word vocabulary
(`working` / `not working` / `could not determine`), because a *diagnostic* has to
be able to say "not working" in a way the status line never does.

So the panel the audit was least likely to look at - the one whose whole subject
is "what is wrong here" - was the one the scan could not reach. **The first
instance of the class the sweep was written to find was in the file it skipped.**
Measured afterwards by re-running the sweep's intent against `STATUS_NOT_WORKING`:
the population is **26 red sites in one file**, and `grep -rl '^STATUS_WORKING ='`
confirms diagnostics is the only panel with its own words at all.

### Two instances, and the second was on the panel's default path

**1. "Conversation checkpoints" - a machine where nothing had been said.**
Its docstring says a missing session directory is *"the normal 'nothing done yet'
state, not a fault"*, and both branches below return red - including the exact
case the sentence names. The section above it says it in prose. **The file
contradicted itself twice, in the same words.**

**2. The three model-server rows - Eyes, Imagine, Memory - on every default
install.** Their docstring says *"a server with no env file was never configured,
and that is a different answer from one that is configured and not answering"* -
and both go red. The Model servers section says it a third time: *"Each may be
asleep, which is a normal state for all three."*

So the panel's own prose was right three times and its code wrong twice, in two
different functions, about two different conditions. **That is the review this
audit has been doing all session** - and the remediation is the same shape in
both, which is why it is worth stating once: **where a docstring and a return
value disagree, measure which one the screen follows.** Here it was the return,
every time, and the prose was the only thing on the side of the person.

### Zero checkpoints and zero configuration are each two facts

| | was | now |
|---|---|---|
| store never created | red | **green** - nothing to rewind |
| store empty | red | **green** - nothing to rewind |
| conversation saved, no checkpoint | red | **red** - rewinding it would silently do nothing |
| store unreadable | *green, counting zero* | **"could not determine"** |
| extra never configured (env absent) | red | **green** - a choice, not a fault |
| extra configured, not answering | red | **red** - somebody wanted it |
| extra answering | green | green |

**The two "red" rows that stay red are the whole fix.** A blanket colour change
would have deleted a real alarm about a saved conversation that cannot be
rewound, and another about a server somebody configured and then stopped - which
is the over-fix this file records for the `get_children` guard. Both have their
own test, in both files, and both were confirmed to fail under the over-fix
mutation.

An unreadable store used to report **a clean count of zero**, which the old code
could not know and which nothing caught. It is `could not determine` now - the
third word of the vocabulary, the one `STATUS_UNKNOWN` exists for.

### And the docstring was wrong about which function knows how to count

`_checkpoint_count` named `conversation_store.list_checkpoints` as *"the one
place that knows how to enumerate them; a probe should use it rather than
reimplementing the glob"*. **`list_checkpoints(root, sid)` is per-session.** The
probe had no conversation id, which is *why* the glob existed. It now asks
`list_sessions` for the ids and `list_checkpoints` for each, so the claim becomes
true rather than aspirational.

**And the probe was about to create the store it asked about.** `list_sessions`
goes through `index()`, which makes the directory; `root.exists()` is checked
first. A read-only diagnostic asking about a never-used store must not be the
thing that brings it into existence, and it would have changed the *next* run's
answer.

### The old fixture described a state the store cannot produce

It wrote two `.ckpt.N.jsonl` files into a directory with no index and asserted
*"in 1 conversation(s)"* - **one**, while writing two files. It passed only
because the old glob counted files and called them conversations. `list_sessions`
reads the index, so a directory of checkpoint files with no index holds **no
conversations at all**: the fixture could never have reached the claim it was
checking. Fixtures now go through `new_session` / `append` / `checkpoint`.

That is also why the first mutation run found **two survivors** - both were the
fixture's shape, not a missing check: `sessions[:1]` (only the first conversation
counted) and `total += 1` (files counted as conversations) left the file green,
because every other case built exactly one conversation. Two tests now carry two.

### 11 mutations, 11 caught, 0 survivors

Both shipped defects restored verbatim, both over-fixes, the unreadable-store
case, the directory guard, both counting mutations, the remedy no longer named,
and a server that is answering reported as down. Run on a **snapshot** at
`/tmp/opencode/snap-diag`, never the shared tree, source restored byte-identical.

### Three harness faults, and every one produced a clean-looking result

1. **Six false cleans.** Forcing `GDK_BACKEND=broadway` with no
   `BROADWAY_DISPLAY` segfaulted before any summary, and the harness counted
   `exit != 0` as **caught** - a table of six passes that measured nothing. A run
   with no summary is `UNMEASURABLE`, never "caught" - the rule
   `MutationDidNotParse` already states in `tools/mutate.py`, and I had it in
   /tmp rather than in the file I was reading it from.
2. **`env -i` strips `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` and `DISPLAY`**, and the same suite
   segfaults at GTK widget construction. Both segfaults read as product failures.
3. **My own script lost its runner loop.** A `str.replace` patch wrote
   `head + body` and dropped everything after the mutations table, so the first
   run printed *nothing* and exited 0. Zero output from a passing harness and
   zero output from a broken one look identical - which is the same statement the
   chunk runner's `INCOMPLETE` makes.

### And I measured my own fix with the wrong instrument, twice

`grep "nothing to rewind yet"` returned **0** in a file that contained the fix,
because the sentence is split across two source lines. The same substring check
then reported my snapshot as unfixed and I nearly re-copied the tree.

**Then it happened again, inside the test I was writing**: I asserted
`"which is a normal state for all three" in inspect.getsource(...)` and it failed
on wording that was two lines away - because **adjacent Python string literals do
not join in raw source**. Whitespace-normalising fixes a split *line*, not a
*literal boundary*. The sentence only exists once evaluated, so the assertion now
reads `_SECTIONS`' own prose - which is what a person reads, which is only what a
test should assert, and which cannot go stale.

**Twice in one day a pattern read as an absence.** The instrument was the problem
both times, and the second one is the more instructive: the first pattern was
wrong on the file, the second was wrong on *Python*.

### Measured, by driving the panel's own row table

`_SECTIONS`, all 22 rows, with `XDG_DATA_HOME` pointed at the repo's own model
cache so the answer is about this machine and not about a directory a probe
invented:

| row | verdict |
|---|---|
| Local model server - selected, not answering | **red** - configured but down |
| Conversation checkpoints | **red** - a real conversation with no checkpoint |
| Screen capture | **red** - every backend failed on this desktop |
| `solve_math` | **red** - `python-symengine` is a hard `depends` |
| vision / embed / imagine servers | **green** - never configured, nothing wrong |
| speech out, microphone, audio path, ffmpeg… | green |

**The first probe run reported four reds, two of which were my own harness.** A

`_speech_in` and part of `_brain` read as broken on a box where both are present.
That is the `fake_bin` `PATH` and `GSETTINGS_BACKEND` lesson in the opposite
direction - **a probe that does not control its environment describes the machine
it ran on, and here the machine did not exist.** Pointed at `cache/data-home`,
`_speech_in` is green and the two reds that remain are real.

**4 red of 22, and each one names its own remedy.** Three concerning an installed
thing that is genuinely not working, and one a hard dependency absent on this
