### The `.pyc` trap, and it was mine

35 stray bytecode files under `usr/` after my own probes. Every command this
session sets `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1`, so it was not a test run - it was the
two ad-hoc probes I wrote with `cat > /tmp/opencode/...` and then ran with the
variable set on the pytest line but not on the probe. Removed by exact path
after listing what would go, nothing tracked, `test_packaging` 28 passed after.
**A red packaging test means "clean `/tmp`" more often than it means "fix the
code"** - and this time it meant neither: it meant "the leaner ran without the
flag it always has".

## A machine configured in the cloud was told it had no model (2026-10-13)

Asked to review the main UI as a newcomer who has cloud and wants to ask
everything. The first thing that render raised is on the main window's most
important line, and it is a question about **who is answering**, which is the
one thing a newcomer looks at to decide whether Chronoa can answer them at all.

    Answers with  No model

`ChronoaWindow._model_word()` reads **only the local registry**:
`local_llm.active()` and the strip's `_model_rows()`. On a machine that
configured a provider, nothing is downloaded, so the registry's answer is always
`""`, the rows fall through to their placeholder row, and the row reads "No
model" **while a provider holds every turn**.

**The app already had the right reader.** `current_llm_kind()` returns
`local`/`cloud`/`none` **from the object holding the turn** - and its own
docstring says why a setting cannot answer it, because the engine is *selected*
and re-decided at startup and by the fallback. It is what
`_note_engine_disagreement` already uses, so the warning and the row were two
answers to one question from two sources. It is now one reader, `_answering_kind`,
used by both.

**"a cloud provider", not the provider's name.** `CloudLLMChain` knows which one
answered, but only *after* a turn - and a row that is empty until somebody asks
is a row that cannot answer the question it exists for on a fresh window. The
specific provider is named by the egress chip and the Privacy panel.

### Two controls, because a fix that cannot be over-applied is not a fix yet

Nothing answering must still read "No model", and a machine with a local model
must not be told its replies come from a provider - **which is the more alarming
of the two wrong answers, because it is the privacy one**. Both are asserted,
and the third-engine control asserts the three engines get three different words
rather than one answer three times.

### 5 mutations, 4 caught, 1 equivalent (documented), 0 survivors

| mutation | |
|---|---|
| the cloud branch gone (**the shipped defect**) | 3 failed |
| **any engine that exists is called a provider (the over-fix)** | 3 failed |
| cloud named as "another model" | 1 failed |
| a raising engine reader propagates | 1 failed |
| the missing-reader guard gone | **equivalent** |

**The equivalent is the finding, and getting to it cost two wrong turns worth
recording.** `_answering_kind` guards the same path twice - an explicit
`if reader is None` and a `try/except` around the call - so deleting either
leaves the other. Deleting **both** is caught, which is what shows the pair is
load-bearing rather than one of them dead.

The first turn was worse: the survivor was reported as a **coverage gap** and it
was a **witness that could not fail**. The test asserted the degradation
through `_model_word`, whose blanket `except` answers `"No model"` whether the
reader works or not - so removing the guard changed nothing the test could see.
**A test that reaches its subject through a caller that swallows exceptions
cannot fail.** The property belongs to the reader, so it is now asked of the
reader, directly, for both faults.

**And the fixture made all three of the cloud tests fail for the wrong reason
twice.** `_model_word` calls `self._answering_kind()`, and a bare
`SimpleNamespace` does not carry methods from the class - so the call raised,
the blanket `except` answered "No model", and the *local-model* control failed
too, which reads exactly like the defect surviving the fix. Same trap as this
file's `Gtk.Popover.__new__` and as `test_model_picker.py`'s, which was written
to record it.

### And what the render could not show

`render_ui.py`'s `main` builds a bare `Gtk.Application`, so there is no engine to
ask and the row still reads "No model" in the capture - **the picture cannot
show this fix**, because the harness builds the one machine the fix is about
wrong. The row is verified by driving the real reader against a stand-in engine,
and a `main:cloud` render target - an app with a `CloudLLMChain` - is the honest
way to see it, and is recorded rather than built here.

## The renderer now blanks the main window and still reports PASS (2026-10-13)

Found while trying to build the `main:cloud` target the cloud-engine fix needed.
Recorded first because it is **live and it will mislead the next person**, who
will be looking at white rectangles and reading them as renders.

    render_ui.py at HEAD (byte-identical, `git diff` empty), 1280x800:
      1 rendered, 0 not.
      opaque 0.2%      <- 183,117 bytes earlier today, 100% opaque

**The same command on the same commit gave 100% opaque earlier in this
session**, so the difference is exhaustion, not code: this pass ran about eight
renders and the broadway pool is 31 numbers. It is the `acquire_display` cascade
this file already records - one slow start poisoning the numbers after it - and
the reason the retry loop exists.

**And nothing reports it.** The PASS column is written by `[[ -s "$out" ]]`: a
file appeared. **A blank PNG is 20,000-odd bytes, so every check the sweep runs
passes**, which is the fourth instance of a capture that photographs less than
its target being called a render. The alpha coverage number is right there in
the image and nothing reads it.

**What this cost, and why it is worth writing down.** I spent the remaining
budget convinced my own change had broken the main window - a new engine on the
render's application stand-in - and only checked it because `main` went blank
too. Reverting the one file I had touched, from HEAD, and re-rendering was the
whole diagnosis: **the renderer was already broken before I started.** The
lesson is the same one this file keeps meeting from new directions, and the
costliest version yet: *the failure was in the instrument, and the instinct was
to doubt the code*. `test_mutation_harness_can_fail.py` exists for this, and the
render harness has no equivalent - which is the actual gap.

**So the rule this leaves, in the form it needs:** **a render target is not
proved by a file appearing.** Alpha coverage and a distinct sha across targets
are the checks that distinguish a picture from a page, and the batch driver does
neither. Adding them is a small change to `render_once` and would have caught
this, the 129,834-byte `cloud-keys` false pass and the 96.2%-transparent main
window with one line each.

### And `main:cloud` is recorded, not built

The target is the right idea and it does not work yet. Setting the stand-in
application's `llm` to an unbuilt `CloudLLMChain` (`__new__`, so `isinstance`
passes without reading every configured key) makes the window capture **0.3%
opaque**. Two forms were tried - its own `elif`, then a flag on the main path -
and both blank, so the cause is the engine object rather than the target's
shape.

**The suspected mechanism, not established:** the window pre-builds every surface
in an idle callback, so a surface raising on an unbuilt chain **aborts the main
loop rather than naming itself**, and no display was free long enough to read
the traceback. `gui/surfaces/model.py:452` reads `getattr(llm, "model", "")`
which an unbuilt chain survives, so the surface that raises is not that one.

**Not shipped**, because a target whose output is a blank page is the defect
this entry is about. What was kept is nothing in `render_ui.py` - it is back at
HEAD - and the window-side fix, which degrades correctly when the application
cannot say which engine is answering, and which is pinned directly against the
reader rather than through a caller that swallows exceptions.

## The gate the render harness never had: a file appearing is not a render (2026-10-13)

The entry above records the live fault. **This is the fix**, and it is the
smallest change in this file that removes a whole class.

`tools/render_ui_batch.sh` decided PASS with:

    [[ -s $out ]]

**A blank PNG is 20,000-odd bytes.** So every check passed on a capture of
nothing, four times over: the 96.2%-transparent main window, the 129,834-byte
`cloud-keys` false pass (which *outranked* a genuine 25,932-byte page on size),
`composer-empty` at 0.3%, and `main` itself blanking at HEAD while the sweep
printed "1 rendered, 0 not".

`render_once` now measures how much of the PNG is actually painted and fails
below `MIN_OPAQUE_PCT` (50, overridable). **The floor is not a guess**: every
genuine render recorded in this repository is 100% opaque and every recorded
false pass is 7.2% or worse, so nothing sits near the line.

**Measured end to end, on the fault itself** - the identical command on the
identical commit:

    before:  1 rendered, 0 not.      (opaque 0.2%)
    after:   0 rendered, 1 not.

**Two rules inside the gate, both from this file's own experience:**

- **A probe that could not measure is not a pass.** Missing Pillow, a truncated
  file, a path that is not a PNG: `_opaque_percent` prints nothing and the gate
  **fails**. The old gate passed all of those, which is the defect.
- **The threshold is read out of the script, not copied.** The test extracts
  `_opaque_percent` and `MIN_OPAQUE_PCT` from the driver rather than restating
  them, because a second copy of a number is `skills_total`, `42/87/70` and
  "105 characters" - three recorded incidents of a value that drifted from the
  code it describes.

### And extracting it was wrong twice before it worked

Both failures presented as *the gate being broken*, which is the trap this
test exists in front of:

1. `chunk.index("PYOPACITY")` finds the heredoc's **opener** `<<'PYOPACITY'`,
   not its terminator, so the extracted body was empty and all three
   measurements came back `None`.
2. Slicing from `_opaque_percent() {` means the chunk **already opens** the
   function - wrapping it again produced
   `_opaque_percent() {_opaque_percent() {` - and stopping before the terminator
   left the heredoc unclosed.

So all three measurement tests failed for reasons in the *test*, and a reader
would reasonably have concluded the gate was wrong. **A check that measures
nothing and a check that is broken produce the same result**, which is why the
positive control exists: `test_a_real_capture_is_above_the_floor` fails too if
the extraction returns nothing for everything, so the negative cannot pass alone.

`tests/test_a_render_target_is_not_a_file_appearing.py` (7), including the
wiring assertions - because **a correct function nothing calls is a dead
control**, the shape this file records for `Registry.register`,
`Gateway.may_execute` and `refused_tools`.

**Not claimed:** an end-to-end *positive*. Every render attempted afterwards
came back blank too, so the pool was still exhausted and the gate was never
shown accepting a real capture through the driver itself - only through the
same measurement code, against a known 99%-opaque PNG. The three population
tests cover the comparison; the driver-level positive needs a pool that has
recovered.

### Correction: the blank renders are NOT pool exhaustion, and the cause is not established

The entry above blames exhaustion. **That was not measured when it was written,
and it is wrong.** Measured, immediately afterwards:

| what I claimed | what is true |
|---|---|
| "~8 renders against a 31-number pool", exhaustion | **2 live daemons, 0 ports held** in the 8080+ band, 17 socket files with nothing listening |
| a concurrent mutation run rewriting the tree | **no `run.lock`, `window.py` byte-identical to HEAD** with the fix in it |

So neither cause holds and `main` **still renders 0.2% opaque at HEAD**. The
cause is unknown.

**The claim got in because it agreed with the conclusion I had already reached.**
That is the same shape as `skills_total`, `42/87/70` and "105 characters" - a
number or a cause produced by a pattern rather than a measurement, then acted on
- and this file's own instruction is *"environmental is a claim, not a verdict"*
and *"a failure list nobody re-measures is worse than no list"*. I did the
re-measure in the wrong direction: having decided the pool was exhausted, I
looked for the pool being exhausted.

**And the second false lead was my own `pgrep`.** `pgrep -f "mutate.py"` matched
the shell command containing that string, so a concurrent mutation run appeared
to be in flight when there was none. This is the recorded `pkill`/`ps | grep`
self-match trap, and **the workspace rule names the bracket guard as the fix for
`grep` and nothing else** - which is why it keeps arriving by a new route.

**What the gate bought anyway, and why the correction matters less than it
looks.** `render_once` measures opacity and says so, so the blank is now reported
as blank. **That is true whatever the cause is** - and it is the property the
render harness was missing independent of this fault. The diagnosis is open; the
check is not.

**What is worth measuring next, in this order** - each a measurement rather than
an inference:

1. **the render log.** `render_once` writes `$SANDBOX/<target>.log` and the
   sandbox is deleted on exit, so the traceback that would name the cause has
   been thrown away on every attempt. **Keeping the log when a target fails**
   is a two-line change and the absence of it is why this entry ends in "not
   established" after four attempts.
2. whether `start_display` reports success while the daemon it started dies -
   the same "a live daemon is a thing to wait for, not a file to delete" shape
   the `rm -f` cascade fixed, asked again from the port side.
3. whether it is time-of-day or load, by rendering the *same* target twice
   minutes apart - which is the control this whole episode lacked.

## What the blank renders actually are (2026-10-13)

The entry two above ends "not established" after four attempts. **It is
established**, and it took one change to find out: **stop deleting the log.**

    Gsk:ERROR:../../../gsk/gskrenderer.c:130:gsk_renderer_dispose:
        assertion failed: (!priv->is_realized)
    Bail out!

**The capture completes and the process then aborts at teardown.** The renderer
prints its `WROTE` line, writes the PNG, and dies in `gsk_renderer_dispose` with
a `GskCairoRenderer` that was never realised. So the PNG on disk is real, valid,
20,000-odd bytes - and blank, because nothing was ever rasterised into it.

That is the **third** recorded instance of a renderer that needs
`Gsk.CairoRenderer.new()` -> `realize(None)` before `render_texture`, and the
first where the abort was visible and nobody was keeping the file that showed it.

**So the previous entry's correction stands and is now explained.** Not pool
exhaustion (0 ports held), not a concurrent mutation run (no lock, `window.py`
byte-identical to HEAD) - and the window *is* being built; it is the rasteriser
that never comes up. `CHRONOA_FORCE_SIZE` and the target are not implicated: the
same commit renders 100% opaque when the display is warm and 0.2% when it is
cold, which is why the control this episode lacked is **render the same target
twice, minutes apart**.

### The change that found it, which is worth more than the finding

`render_once` wrote the renderer's stderr to `$SANDBOX/<target>.log` and the
sandbox was deleted when the sweep exited. **Four consecutive attempts at this
diagnosis produced nothing, and the reason is not that the evidence was hard to
read - it is that nobody kept it.** The log is now copied beside its output, so
a failed target leaves `<target>.log` next to the blank PNG.

**A diagnostic nobody can read is not a diagnostic**, and this file has several
checks whose failure mode is silence - the alpha gate added above is one, and
this log is the other. Both were the same omission: a thing that could have told
the truth had nowhere to be read.

### What to do about the abort, in order

1. **Realise the renderer before capturing** - `Gsk.CairoRenderer.new()` then
   `realize(None)`, which this file's own "Rendering the UI to a PNG" section
   prescribes and which the capture path appears to skip. The abort names the
   function and the missing call.
2. **and treat the abort as the failure.** A renderer that bails after writing
   should not leave a file the sweep can count. `Bail out!` is on stderr and
   nothing reads stderr, so a process that died mid-capture and one that
   finished look identical from outside - which is the same shape as the
   `-rs` flag finding this file records, where a check stopped looking and still
   printed a tally.

**Not done here**, and the reason is that a renderer fix needs a warm display to
prove it, and this pass has not had one since the pool went cold.


## The grammar is real and it is enforced - and it buys form, not decisions (2026-10-13)

The three-arm decoder run `AGENTS.md` prescribed for two entries and never ran.
Arms 1 and 2 already existed (`+greedy`, `+greedy+constrained`); **the control
arm did not**, and building it is most of what this entry is about. Before any
score, the lever itself was verified, because a grammar that was silently off
would have produced a tie that read as "the grammar bought nothing".

### The proof, and what it shows

`llama-server` given `response_format` whose schema allows exactly one value,
and a user asking for something else:

| | what came back |
|---|---|
| grammar **off** | prose: *"I don't have access to real-time weather data..."* |
| grammar **on** | `{"tool": "get_datetime"}` - the **only legal value**, for a question about weather |

**So enforcement is not a claim, it is measured**, and it produced the finding
this run was worth doing for. The grammar forced the model to name a tool it had
**already decided against**. It constrained *form* completely and *choice* not at
all.

That is the mechanism behind the caution two entries up, and it is sharper than
"constrained decoding may distort intent" (arXiv:2604.06066, 2510.17376). Those
papers say constraining the decoder can cost you something. This says **exactly
what the constraint buys and cannot buy**: it makes every answer well-formed and
leaves every answer possibly wrong. A grammar turns "no tool called" into "a tool
called"; it does not turn the wrong tool into the right one.

Which is why `task_eval` scores **the tool and the arguments** and never schema
validity. Schema validity is the thing the grammar guarantees, so measuring it
would measure the thing under test.

### Why the control arm had to be built rather than reasoned about

`+greedy+constrained` and `+greedy` differ in **three** ways at once - two-step
prompt, schema, and enforcement - so their difference measures none of them
alone. The control arm removes two of the three:

| arm | prompt | payload | runnable |
|---|---|---|---|
| `+greedy` | llama-server's own tool calling | native | already existed |
| `+greedy+constrained` | two steps, schema in prose | `response_format` -> grammar | already existed |
| `+greedy+request` | **the same two steps, the same schema in prose** | **no `response_format`** | **new here** |

**The single variable is the grammar.** Without enforcement the prompt is the only
channel, so the schema is written into it as prose (`_shape_request`) and the
model reads the same shape either way. That equality used to be a promise in a
docstring, which is not checkable; `_arm_prompt` was lifted out of `_constrained
for exactly that reason, and
`test_the_control_arm_is_the_grammar_arm_plus_a_suffix` now asserts the control
prompt **starts with** the grammar prompt and differs only by that suffix.

### Two wrong calls of my own, both caught only by reading output

The first version of `TestTheTwoArmsAreNotBothOn` called `make_llm`, which does
not exist, inside a bare `except: pass` - so all three tests read the **defaults**,
and `test_plain_greedy_has_neither` **passed vacuously**. The second called
`build_llm` with one argument when it takes two; a guard that only reclassified
`AttributeError` let the `TypeError` through and the defaults were read again.
The lesson is the specific one: **the only test in the class that could have
caught it asserts an absence, and absence is exactly what a broken harness
produces.** A test that passes when the thing it names is missing is not a test.
Both are now `module.build_llm(config, "")` with no exception handling at all.

### A third, and it was mine in the tool rather than the test

`tools/three_arm.py` counted its population by splitting `--cases` and counting
the **strings**, so a run reported `5 cases` when the file holds 225 and only
**three** of those ids exist (`volume` is not a case). Every denominator it had
ever printed was wrong, and `3/5` was really `3/3`. The tool now loads
`eval_cases.json`, prints `N case(s) of 225 in the file` **before starting a
server**, and pins the resolved ids into argv so what was asked for is what runs.

**Stated plainly: a summary line that reads the same for 3 cases and 220 is a
reporting defect, not a formatting choice**, and this one survived a complete
dry run because the dry run also printed the wrong number.

### State of the run

3 cases: `+greedy` **3/3**, `+greedy+constrained` **3/3**, `+greedy+request`
**2/3** - which is 3 cases and settles nothing, and is reported here only so the
denominator correction is not mistaken for the final number. **The 220-case run
is in flight.** The arm-to-arm numbers go in when it lands; the enforcement proof
above does not depend on it.

17 tests, 10 mutations - 10 caught, 0 survivors, 0 equivalent, 0 stale witnesses.
The two mutations worth naming are **"the control arm enforces anyway"** and
**"the dispatch ignores which arm it is on"**, because between them they cover
the two ways the run could have reported a grammar comparison while measuring
nothing: the flag right and the wire wrong, and the wire wrong with no test on
it. The dispatch is driven end to end against a real `_Local` instance with
`chat_message` patched, so the grammar that would have leaked shows up as a
failed test rather than as a slightly lower score.

### Correction: the renderer IS realised, and the abort is not the cause of the blank

The entry above says the capture "dies in `gsk_renderer_dispose` with a
`GskCairoRenderer` that was **never realised**". **That is backwards, and the
assertion text says so:**

    gsk_renderer_dispose: assertion failed: (!priv->is_realized)

A failed assertion means the condition was **false** - so `priv->is_realized`
is **true**. The renderer *was* realised, which is also what the code says:
`_capture` calls `Gsk.CairoRenderer.new()` and then `renderer.realize(None)` one
line later, and this repository's own "Rendering the UI to a PNG" section
prescribes exactly that pair. I read the assertion's *content* as its
*conclusion*.

**And the ordering rules the abort out as the cause anyway.** The log is three
lines in this order:

    WROTE
    **
    Gsk:ERROR:... gsk_renderer_dispose ... Bail out!

`WROTE` is printed immediately after `texture.save_to_png(path)` returns, and the
file is on disk and non-empty. **So the capture completed and the process died
afterwards, at interpreter teardown** - and the PNG is blank for some other
reason entirely. A crash after a successful write cannot be why the write is
empty.

**So the state is: the blank is confirmed, the cause is not.** Reproduced twice
from a cold pool, identical log, identical 0.2%. What is *not* established is
what the texture contains and why.

**The next measurement, and it is a one-line probe rather than another render:**
what `_deepest_node()` returns, and what its allocation is, on a cold display.
The `node is None` and `texture is None` branches both print and both *did not*
fire - so a node and a texture existed and the texture was blank, which points
at the node rather than the rasteriser. `_capture` prints neither the node's
type nor its allocation, and **a probe that reports only success cannot
distinguish "painted" from "emptied"** - the same class as the blank-image probe
this file records needing a positive control.

**Recorded rather than fixed**, because a fix to the capture path cannot be
verified on this box while every display is cold, and an unverified fix to the
one thing every render depends on is worse than the gap.


## Four abstracts read whole, and they say the thing the probe measured (2026-10-13)

The `Result.abstract` field added earlier today is now carrying its weight. The
papers this file had recorded **by title only** - because the old tool truncated
the abstract to a tail - have been read. The result is not a list of cautions
any more; it is one finding from four directions, and **it is the finding the
grammar probe measured on this box**.

### The alignment-tax paper (arXiv:2604.06066) describes the probe's result

*From Hallucination to Structure Snowballing*, Qwen3-8B, Outlines-based
constrained decoding over structured reflection. In its own words: imposing
structural constraints **"does not improve self-correction performance"**; it
instead triggers a failure mode they name **structure snowballing**, where **"the
cognitive load required to satisfy strict formatting rules pushes the model into
formatting traps"**. And the sentence that matches this repository's probe
exactly: the agent **"achieves near-perfect superficial syntactic alignment yet
fails to detect or resolve deeper semantic errors."**

The probe measured: schema allowing exactly one value, question about the
weather, model answers `get_datetime` - the one value it was allowed, having
already decided the question was not about the time. **Near-perfect superficial
syntactic alignment, no semantic gain.** That paper reached it on
self-correction at 8B; this reached it on tool choice at **1.7B**. Same finding,
independent route. It is no longer a caution imported from elsewhere - it is a
prediction this box confirmed.

### The control arm was predicted to be where the effect lives

*Structured Output Collapses Answer Diversity Across 44 Language Models*
(arXiv:2607.18476), read whole this time. The 31 prompts, 44 models, and the
numbers: modal answer **41% -> 64%**, distinct answers **52 -> 36**, mean
answer-choice surprisal **1.80 -> 1.58 bits**, all from **"Reply with JSON
only"** - *no schema, no enforcement, just the request*.

The clause that decided the design of `+greedy+request`: **"Enforcing the schema
at the decoder (response_format) compresses no further than the request (-0.03
bits)."** The collapse lives in the model's response to the **register**, not in
the decoder. So if there is any effect to find at all, the control arm is where
it is, and a grammar-only measurement would have read as a decoder result what
the paper says is a register result.

**And the direction of that effect is against a tool chooser specifically.**
They call it **"a sharpener, not a re-indexer"** - the plain-chat answer survives
in 28 of 31 categories - and JSON **"shifts 53% of a model's stable chat defaults,
mostly back to the crowd"**. For a tool chooser the mode is **the most common
tool**, not the right one. That is precisely the failure `tool_select`'s plain
word overlap already produces, arriving from the other direction: a collapsed
distribution falls back on the mode.

Also worth keeping: the compression is **format-specific** - JSON -0.22 bits
(p=.0002), XML -0.19 (p=.002), **absent for YAML and CSV**, and **reversed** for
an arbitrary bracket wrapper (+0.13, p=.009) - which is why they weigh it toward
tool-use post-training.

### AdapTrack's numbers, now read rather than cited

arXiv:2510.17376 in full: constrained decoding **"distorts the model's output
intent, forcing it to produce code that may satisfy the constraint but does not
match the development intent and is therefore incorrect."** Improvement from
*not* distorting, over constrained decoding: **360.87%** on a synthetic API
completion dataset, **38.93%** on a real-world one they collected, **7.84%**
HumanEval, **6.42%** MBPP. The earlier entry quoted these from a summary; they
are now read from the abstract.

### The actionable finding, and it is not the grammar

**Schema-Key Wording as an Instruction Channel** (arXiv:2604.14862) - read whole:
schema-key tokens **enter the autoregressive context** and act as an instruction
channel; on GSM8K and Math500 across **seven** models, **changing only schema-key
wording substantially affects accuracy, with both positive and negative effects**,
and prompt-level and schema-level instructions interact **non-additively**.

That is a cheap, untested lever this repository is sitting on. Chronoa's tool
argument keys are English words chosen once (`place`, `when`, `text`, `action`,
`seconds`) and **never A/B'd**. Given tool choice is the binding constraint and
the grammar demonstrably cannot touch it, the schema's *wording* is the one
channel in the literature that moves accuracy **without** a training run and
**without** constraining the decoder. It is also the cheapest thing in this entry
to test: same instrument, same cases, rename keys, measure.

### What is read and what is not

**Read: the four abstracts, in full, through the shipped tool.** These are
abstracts - an author's own summary of their own experiments - not the papers.
Not read: methods, tables, ablations, the actual per-task numbers behind the
percentages, or the limitations sections. Every percentage above is quoted from
an abstract and none is verified against a table. Nothing here should be read as
a reproduction; it is a survey of claims, and the claims are attributed.

## The mutation set the other session ported had three witnesses the harness could not see (2026-10-13)

While fixing the anchor bug below I found `tools/mutate.py diagnostics` reporting
**7 mutations, 5 caught, 0 survivors, 2 unmeasurable** - and the two unmeasurable
were **the shipped defect and the over-fix**, the two most important claims in the
set. `MutationDidNotParse: 1 warning, 1 error`, which is the runner *correctly*
refusing to guess.

**The cause was an anchor that ended mid-line.** The set's two key mutations
replaced

        if not binary:
            # **Never configured is not a fault**

with `if False:`. The anchor stopped at `not a fault**` with **no trailing
newline**, so `str.replace` produced

        if False:** - which this docstring says two

and the corpus never collected. **The runner caught it and reported it as
unmeasurable rather than as caught** - which is the whole point of that code path,
and the reason a `survivor` here would have been a *false clean* of exactly the
kind this entry is about.

Extending both anchors to the end of the comment's first line takes the set from
`5 caught, 2 unmeasurable` to **7 caught, 0 survivors, 0 unmeasurable**.

### Then the harness told me the same thing about three of those mutations

`tests/test_mutation_harness_can_fail.py` went red - not on the mutations, on the
*checker*:

> 3 mutation(s) name no test and are not flagged equivalent, so the inventory
> reports them as SURVIVORS - indistinguishable from a guard with no witness at
> all

The three all name `_GREEN` - a module-level
`_GREEN = "test_a_server_setup_never_configured_is_not_a_fault"`. The validator
counts witnesses by reading `expect` elements and keeping `ast.Constant`, so an
`ast.Name` reads as **no witness at all**. The three entries name a witness each
time.

**A checker that cannot see a correct spelling is the `skills_total` mistake
inside a validator.** The two wrong ways out would both have been plausible:
inline five copies of the long test name, or flag a live guard `equivalent`. The
right one is to resolve the alias - which is one dict of module-level
`NAME = "literal"` bindings, built before the walk.

### And a second validator, and the shadowing bug I wrote fixing the first

`TestEveryMutationEitherHasAWitnessOrSaysWhyItCannotHaveOne` also flagged
`wizard_mark.py`: an `"equivalent": True` with the full reason written in a
**comment** above it and no `why` key. That is verbatim the failure the test's own
docstring records - *"a documented equivalent ... explained themselves in prose
where no tool reads it"* - already fixed for `history.py`, and here again in the
concurrent session's file. The prose is preserved and the `why` now carries it.

**My fix for the first bug had my own second bug in it.** The name map was
written as a comprehension:

    names = {n.id: n.value for n in tree.body
             if isinstance(n, ast.Assign)
             and isinstance(n.value, ast.Constant)
             for n in n.targets if isinstance(n, ast.Name)}

`for n in ... for n in ...` **rebinds the same name inside its own
comprehension**, so the value half reads `.value` off an `ast.Name` and raises
`AttributeError`. Distinct loop names, stated in a comment rather than left for
the next reader. **pyflakes is clean on a shadowed comprehension** - it is a
runtime fault, and only running the test found it.

### A third gate refused to run, and the lock it named was stale

`tests/test_mutation_harness_can_fail.py` then exited with *"a mutation run (pid
413487) is rewriting the source tree right now"* - and `CHRONOA_MUTATION_RUN` was
**unset**, `build/mutate/run.lock` did not exist, and pid 413487 was gone. So the
refusal was **a stale lock file whose owner had already exited**, and the suite
would have sat refused for a holder that no longer existed. It is recorded rather
than fixed: the guard is doing its job (refuse rather than read mutated code),
and a lock whose owner dies without releasing it is the same class the runner
already handles by *taking it over and saying so* - here it just said nothing.
**53 passed** once the lock was gone.

### And a mutation set that belonged in the repo, not in `/tmp`

The checkpoint-row fix had a working mutation set in `/tmp/opencode/mut_ckpt.py`
and none in `tools/mutations/`. This file's own rule is that a harness in `/tmp`
is lost when the session ends, and **eight were lost this way on 2026-10-11**. It
is `tools/mutations/checkpoints.py` now, and running it found what the /tmp
version had not:

| mutation | verdict |
|---|---|
| a never-created store is a fault | caught |
| an empty store is a fault | caught |
| **a conversation with no checkpoint is fine too** | caught |
| an unreadable store reads as a clean zero | caught |
| the probe creates the store it asks about | caught |
| only the first conversation counted | caught |
| the count is conversations, not files | caught |
| the store's own reader re-inlined | **equivalent** |

**8 mutations, 7 caught, 0 survivors, 1 equivalent, 0 unmeasurable.** The
equivalent is documented rather than dropped: `list_checkpoints` *is* that glob
plus the same `int()` parse, so swapping it changes nothing observable - which is
the honest statement, and a reason to keep the store's reader rather than a claim
that a witness exists.

**Two of my own `expect` lists were wrong and the run said so.** One named
`test_a_saved_checkpoint_is_reported_with_its_conversation` against the counting
mutation - a fixture with one conversation and one checkpoint, where
`total += 1` and `total += len(nums)` are the same number. It was reported
**"NOT caught by"**, which is the over-claiming this file records for
`asleep_state`: a witness that passes either way is worse than a missing one,
because it reads as coverage.

### The anchors, and the one that rotted while I fixed another

Three anchors in `checkpoints.py` were wrong on the first run and the runner
reported each by name - `occurs 0 times ... not once`. Two were **indentation**
(`if not root.exists():` is at 4 spaces here, and `return STATUS_WORKING` at 8,
not 12 - I transcribed them from the function's deeper nesting), and the fix path
for both was the same: read the block from the file rather than from the design.
**`--check-anchors` is the half that costs nothing and it caught all three before
a test ran.**

Final state: **58 sets, 473 anchors of 471 declared mutations, all match the
code**; **651 witnesses across 58 sets, all resolve to a real test id**.

## The whole-population sweep, and why a stub-built one reports the stub (2026-10-13)

The entry above found that the absence-as-fault sweep was scoped to
`common.STATUS_*` and could not see `diagnostics`. The obvious follow-up is the
**complete** population: build every surface, read every status row, classify.

**It ran, and it measured the stub.** All 34 surfaces built and every row printed,
and the answers were largely *"Ready"* - including `driving`, whose red dot this
file has already measured twice as real ("No display this driver can measure").
The difference is that each row was built with `types.SimpleNamespace()` as the
app, and `common._permitted(app)` reads `app.config` - so a stub has no settings,
the gates cannot be read, and the rows answer differently than they do on a
machine. `model` reported `unknown - no settings object` for the same reason.

**So a sweep over stub-built surfaces is a measurement of the stub**, and the
deduction it supports is zero. That is the `fake_bin` `PATH`,
`GSETTINGS_BACKEND`, scratch-`XDG_DATA_HOME` and `keyfile` lessons arriving from a
fifth direction - and this is the one where the *instrument was the finding*,
because two of the four rows above are ones this file records as correct and one
is a measured red.

Two things the honest run does establish:

- **`export` reads `Ready`.** The fix at the top of this stretch is visible in the
  same instrument, which is the value of running it even with the limitation.
- **`daemon` reads `off (background-mode-enabled)`** - consent off, grey, correct.

### And the two panels that would answer it cannot be rendered here at all

`panel:driving` and `panel:model` were re-rendered to look at them properly, and
both came back **byte-identical**, 31,882 bytes, sha `1cca6443fd2e`, **0% opaque
and 99.2% partial**. Two different panels producing one photograph is this file's
recorded false-pass signature, and the batch correctly reported `0 rendered, 2
not`. With `VERBOSE=1` the cause is named and it is the harness, not the page:

    Gsk:ERROR:../../../gsk/gskrenderer.c:130:gsk_renderer_dispose:
      assertion failed: (!priv->is_realized)

A renderer crash on dispose. Neither panel uses `Adw.EntryRow`,
`Gtk.SearchEntry` or `Adw.StatusPage`, so it is not the editable-widget class this
file already documents. **Recorded as an open limitation, not as a finding**: no
claim is available about `driving` and `model` from a render here, and the sweep
could not answer for them either.

### What the population actually is, and what is known about it

| surface | known state | from |
|---|---|---|
| `diagnostics` (22 rows) | 4 red, all genuine, each naming its remedy | driven through its own `_SECTIONS` |
| `export` | Ready | the fix at the top of this stretch |
| `daemon` | `off`, consent off | this sweep |
| everything else that reads `app.config` | **unmeasured here** | a stub app changes the answer |

`diagnostics` is the panel this audit can actually measure, because its probes
are **zero-argument by design** - *"so this asks the engines directly rather than
reading `app.stt`"*. That is the property that makes it auditable, and it is why
the one genuinely reachable population was worth measuring completely.

**The next pass wants a config stub rather than a `SimpleNamespace`** - the
`gsettings_env` fixture already builds one, and a sweep that substitutes it for
the app would measure the panels instead of the harness. That is a real change
with its own review, and it is named here rather than half-built.

## The 36 files in the repo root are conversation ids, and the shipped code does not write them (2026-10-13)

The question had been asked three times without an answer, so it was answered by
measurement instead: **trace the writer**. The names are the lead, and the lead
decoded on the first try.

**`conversation_store._new_id()` is `strftime("%Y%m%d-%H%M%S") + "-" +
secrets.token_hex(2)`** - and `token_hex(2)` is **exactly four hex characters**.
Every one of the 36 filenames matches that form. So these are **conversation
session ids**, and whatever wrote them pointed the conversation store at the
**repository root**.

That narrows the writer to a caller of `new_session(root)` with a relative root,
and rules out most of the field by measurement rather than by reasoning:

| candidate | measured |
|---|---|
| `Assistant()` with no `session_path` | writes **nothing** - `_record` guards on `is not None` |
| `session_dir()` itself | resolves to `data_home()/shani-chronoa/sessions`, never the CWD |
| `tests/test_conversations.py` | its `root` fixture sets `XDG_DATA_HOME` to `tmp_path` |
| `tests/test_assistd_sayri_harvest.py` | the fixture is an **in-memory list**; the file that matched `"content": "second"` writes no file |
| `tests/test_conversation_store.py` | writes to the `tmp_path` fixture |
| `gui/surfaces/compare.py`'s `_store_root` | read-only; it resolves a path and never creates one |

**And the strongest lead, measured rather than argued.** `tests/test_compare_surface.py`
is the test that calls `store.new_session(root)` and is **mine**, from the Compare
panel landed 23 minutes after the burst. All three of its commits - `3bc852e`,
`2b7d099`, `96791d8` - use `tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="chronoa-compare-")`, which is
**absolute**, so the committed code cannot have written them. Running the file and
`test_conversations.py` against the live tree:

    junk files before: 36
    40 passed, 1 warning in 3.14s
    junk files after : 36      delta 0

**So the shipped tests do not leak, and the writer was a local draft that was
changed before it was committed.** That is the most likely reading and it is not
proved: a draft exists in no commit and in no reflog, so there is nothing left to
read.

### Where the trace stops, stated rather than dressed up

- All 36 were written in **one ~60-second burst**, `23:36:35` to `23:37:00` on
  Oct 12, and **nothing has been created since** - zero in the following 15 hours.
  So a filesystem watch cannot fire, and that is why the trace is by evidence
  rather than by interception.
- The content is `{"role": "user", "content": "hello"}` followed by
  `{"role": "user", "content": "second"}` - **two user turns and no assistant
  reply**. A round-trip fixture does not look like that; a probe that only calls
  `append()` twice does.
- Two files in the tree contain `"content": "second"` and **neither writes a
  file**: `test_conversation_store.py` uses `"first"`/`"second"` and a `tmp_path`,
  and `test_assistd_sayri_harvest.py` uses `"first"`/`"second"` in memory. The
  word `hello` pairs with `"first"`, not with `"second"`, in both.

**So the writer was most likely an ad-hoc probe of mine from that stretch, not
shipped code** - which is the same conclusion the `code_hl` entry reaches from the
other direction, where a module read as unwired for ninety seconds because the
other session was mid-write.

**This resolves the original decision without a decision.** The files are not
fixture data anyone needs - they are the debris of a probe, they are **not**
gitignored so a bare `git add -A` takes all 36, and nothing in the tree reads
them. Removing them by exact path is the third of the three options offered, and
it is now the one the evidence supports; the writer is dead (zero in 15 hours) so
nothing will re-create them.

**The habit the entry is really about, and it is the fourth time in this file:**
an agent probe that writes where the repository lives is a *write the person did
not ask for*, exactly like the test that wrote the real keyfile and the probes
that left `.pyc` under `usr/`. Every one of those was found by listing what
changed and asking, not by reading code - and this one survived three questions
because **there was nothing to read**: the writer was never committed.

## The "blank" main window is not blank, and the gate I added would have rejected every good render (2026-10-13)

Three entries above chase the blank `main` capture through pool exhaustion, a
mutation run, and an unrealised `GskCairoRenderer`. **All three were wrong, and
the answer was in the file all along - nobody opened it.** The alpha histogram
of `main`, measured:

    alpha 25  -> 51,958 samples (80% of the image)
    alpha 140 ->  8,011
    alpha 151 ->  1,677
    alpha   0 ->    540

**Not one pixel in the window is at 255.** So the sweep was photographing a
painted picture and the gate from `e918a9c` was calling it 0% opaque, because it
counted `alpha == 255` - which is stricter than "painted" by a factor of a
hundred, and which **would have refused every genuine render of this app**.
It was a false negative shipped as a fix, and it is corrected: the measure is
now `alpha > 0`. The 7 tests still reject the blank and accept the painted one,
which is the only reason to believe the correction rather than trust it.

### What the picture actually is

Rendered and **looked at**, not measured: a rounded orange frame, pale inside,
nothing in it. Chronoa's accent (237,128,89) at 8,000 samples. So `main` is not
a photograph of nothing - it is a photograph of **one rounded rectangle**.

### The probe that says so is now shipped in `render_ui.py`

`_print_capture_state` runs before every capture and prints the screen geometry,
the window's allocation, mapped/realized, descendant counts, and how late the
capture actually fired. Measured, four runs:

    CAPTURE main 5137ms mapped=True realized=True alloc=1024x768
           asked=1280x800 screen=1024x768 descendants=948 mapped_descendants=528

**Three facts fall out, and each kills a theory:**

- **`descendants=948 mapped_descendants=528`.** The tree is populated and mapped.
  *Captured too early* is refuted - there was something to photograph.
- **`screen=1024x768`, and `broadwayd` has no size option.** The window came up
  1024x768 when 1280x800 was asked for. **This retires a claim two entries
  above**: that the `state:` branch "ignores `CHRONOA_FORCE_SIZE`". It honours it;
  the screen overrules it. `state:` was never the problem.
- **The PNG is 1280x800 anyway**, because `main` does not pass `own_size` - so the
  capture photographs a 1024x768 window into a 1280x800 frame. `render_once` now
  prints a note when the two differ, above the alpha gate rather than below it,
  because a blank capture is exactly when the size matters most.

**Also measured, and not what the comment says:** the capture fires at
**5137-5439ms**, not the 3500ms it is armed with. The twenty-panel idle chain at
`PRIORITY_DEFAULT_IDLE` - one panel per turn, each running real probes - delays
it by ~1.7s. The `settle = 3500` comment's "measures at about two seconds" was
true on 2026-10-08 and is now wrong; the number belongs to the machine it was
measured on, not to the constant.

### Two of my own probes were broken, in the same commit that exists to stop it

- `getattr(im.size, "0", "")` - `im.size` is a **tuple**. So the size check
  measured nothing on every file, `[[ -n $got_w ]]` was always false, and it
  never printed. **A check that cannot measure passed silently**, which is the
  exact failure the alpha gate exists to prevent, committed in the same change.
- `display.get_n_monitors()` does not exist on `GdkBroadwayDisplay`; it raised
  `AttributeError` inside `_render` and killed the capture it was measuring. **A
  probe that can raise is a probe that can destroy what it is measuring**, so it
  is now a plain read in a `try`-free path that cannot take the render down.

Both were found by reading the output, not by reasoning about it. **And one of my
own commands truncated the evidence that would have shown the first** - `ls -la |
head -4` cut off the very file I was about to conclude did not exist.

### Not established

**Why the node contains one rounded rectangle and not 948 widgets.** The tree is
mapped and populated, so the children exist and the snapshot does not carry them.
That is the open question, and it is now a question rather than four wrong
answers.

## Alpha was the wrong question twice; the UI still cannot be photographed (2026-10-13)

Opening the files settled it. `state:composer-empty` is a **pure white
rectangle** - 26,589 bytes and nothing on it - and the `alpha > 0` gate shipped
one commit earlier scored it 100% and reported it rendered.

**Three measures, and only the third was right:**

| measure | `main` | white page | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| `alpha == 255` | 0% - **refused a real render** | 100% | false negative |
| `alpha > 0` | ~99% | 100% - **passed a blank page** | false positive |
| contrast against background | 4% | 4% | correct |

Alpha says a pixel *exists*. It says nothing about whether anything was drawn
**into** it. `_content_percent` now takes the most common colour in the sample as
the background by definition and asks how much of the image is something else.
A transparent page and a white page both score 0; the orange-framed `main`
scores 4; a real window scores well above the floor.

**Measured on the real targets with the driver's own function:**

    main.png                        4% content
    state:composer-empty.png        4% content
    floor                           5%

**So the gate is right and the pictures are empty**, and this is now an honest
"not rendered" rather than a confident PASS. `tests/test_a_render_target_is_not_a_file_appearing.py`
(8) asserts all three of those rows, including the white page that `alpha > 0`
passed - and the floor's own upper bound, because a floor only the best pictures
clear turns every hard target into a failure and a check that fails on
everything stops being read.

### What this means for a UI review

**The main window cannot be photographed yet, and it is a capture fault rather
than a UI fault.** The probe says the tree is populated and mapped -
`descendants=948 mapped_descendants=528` - so 528 mapped widgets exist and the
snapshot carries none of them, only the window's rounded background. A newcomer
looking at `main` sees an empty orange frame.

**Every UX finding recorded so far about the main window is unverified**, because
every one of them came from reading code or from the one earlier capture, and the
current capture shows no content to confirm any of it. They stay marked as
unverified rather than being dressed up as observations.

### The retry logic also lost a good first attempt

Both files were written on the **first** attempt (15:26, 23,374 and 19,330
bytes) and the verdict came from the **second** (15:28), which wrote nothing and
reported "no file written". So the sweep discards a successful render in favour
of a later empty one - **the same class as the original `[[ -s $out ]]` bug, one
level up**: the decision is made from the last attempt rather than from whether
a picture was ever obtained. Unfixed here; it is the next thing to change, and
the change is to score the best attempt rather than the final one.

## The blank main window was a diagnostic probe raising inside the capture path (2026-10-13)

Three entries above chase `main` coming back blank through pool exhaustion, a
concurrent mutation run, and an unrealised `GskCairoRenderer`, and the last of
them ends **"the blank is confirmed, the cause is not"**. It is now known, and
none of the three theories was right.

    File "render_ui.py", line 352, in _print_capture_state
      total, mapped, capped = _count_descendants(widget)
    NameError: name '_count_descendants' is not defined

`_count_descendants` **is defined** - and the traceback says the *call* was at
line **352** while the definition sits at **347** today. `render_ui.py` is
modified in the working tree: **the probe was mid-edit when the render ran**, so
an undefined helper raised inside `_render` before any capture happened. That is
the `code_hl` shape - a tree in motion, and an absence measured against it
measures the author's progress - and the fourth time this session that a
confident reading about the tree was contradicted by re-measuring.

**A probe that can raise is a probe that can destroy what it is measuring**, which
this file states about `display.get_n_monitors()` two entries up; this is the
same defect in the function written to replace it.

**And the fix for finding it was made earlier the same hour.** `render_once`
writes the renderer's stderr to `$SANDBOX/<target>.log` and the sandbox is deleted
when the sweep exits; `_keep_log` now copies it beside the output. Four
attempts at this diagnosis had produced nothing because **nobody kept the file
that showed it** - the first sweep after that change put the traceback on disk.

**`main` now renders: 30,870 bytes at 17% content**, the first real picture of
the main window in this repository's history. At the window's own 460x640 it
shows the orb, "Ready", the model row, all eight organ lights, the shortcut
buttons and the composer. So the window was never the problem; the instrument was,
which is the direction this file keeps meeting.

## Three defects in the render driver, and the one that printed a lie (2026-10-13)

Fixed in `tools/render_ui_batch.sh`. All three were measured by running the
driver, and all three are the same shape: **the verdict came from the last thing
that happened rather than from the best evidence available.**

1. **Both attempts wrote to `$out` and nothing removed it between them**, so only
   one picture could survive and the survivor was whichever ran last - arbitrary,
   where `render_once`'s own return value already carries the score that would
   order them.
2. **`recycle_display` ran after both attempts** - **ten lines below a comment
   saying** *"a second attempt against the same exhausted display cannot
   succeed"*. The paragraph described the fix and the code did the opposite.
   This is the `rm -f` cascade this driver already records, in a different
   function, and the lesson is the file's own: **a paragraph explaining why
   something is dangerous is not a control.**
3. **The FAIL line said `no file written` whatever had happened.** Measured live:
   `FAIL  main  no file written` with **23,374 bytes** sitting in the output
   directory. The picture was *rejected* - 4% content against a 5% floor - and
   "no file written" sends the reader looking for a missing file instead of a
   rejected one. **The gate that introduced the measurement is what made the
   sentence wrong**, and it was the driver's own absence-shaped wrong answer.

Each attempt is now scored by `_content_percent`, the display is recycled
**between** them, and the best picture becomes *the* artefact whether or not it
clears the floor - so the FAIL line can quote what it measured.

### The fix itself had three defects, and running it found all three

- **The FAIL printed twice.** My replacement's span ended at `recycle_display`,
  and the original `printf` sat *after* it, so the measured line and the stale
  one both fired. Found by reading the run's own output, not the diff.
- **Attempt litter.** The losing attempt was left on disk beside the winner, so
  the output directory held two pictures per target. Now removed; the winning
  attempt's `.tryN.log` is kept, because a log named for the attempt that
  produced the picture beats one named for the target.
- **I claimed "erased a good attempt" before measuring it.** The surviving file
  scores **4%**, below the floor - so the gate was right about it and "good" was
  never established. **Best-of-two** is still the right behaviour (arbitrary is
  not best, and the score is available), but the justification I wrote was not
  the justification the run supports, and it is corrected here rather than left.

### One observation, open, and not claimed as a defect

The shortcut hints - `widgets.py:1044`, *"Ctrl+K for anything else · Ctrl+F to
find in this conversation · ? for what Chronoa can do"* - are appended to
`TranscriptView._rows` **at construction**, so a fresh view does hold them and
`test_shortcuts_are_discoverable` reads a widget that really contains the text.
**They are not visible in the first render of the main window**, whose transcript
region is blank. Whether the window seeds a turn, the scroller gives the row no
height, or the row is simply not reached, is **not established** - and a finding
whose cause is unmeasured is the thing this file records most often.

Anchors: **60 sets, 495 anchors, all still match.**

## The shortcut list read as a paragraph, because five subtitles wrapped (2026-10-13)

Rendered `shortcuts` and looked at it. **Five of the eleven rows in "General"
had their accelerator on a line of its own, hard against the left edge**, under
a description - while the six rows whose subtitle happened to be short kept it
right-aligned beside the title:

    In-app browser          Shift Ctrl U          <- orphaned, far left
    Show or hide the panels     F9                <- orphaned
    Show or hide the Now rail  F10                <- orphaned
    The body register       Shift Ctrl B          <- orphaned
    Hands-free listening     Shift Ctrl W          <- orphaned
    Set Chronoa up          Shift Ctrl S          <- orphaned

So the column that makes a shortcut list read as a list existed for exactly the
rows that had the least to say. That is the mode strip's **"a menu item is a
name, not a sentence"** arriving in a different widget, and like that one it is
invisible to every check that does not look - the rows carry correct text, the
accelerators are registered, and `test_about.py` passed throughout.

**Cause, measured on libadwaita 1.9.1:** `Adw.ShortcutsItem` keeps the
accelerator right-aligned beside the title until the subtitle wraps, and then
drops it below the description. The fix is the subtitle.

**The budget is the table's own break, not a number chosen to pass.** Eleven of
the sixteen subtitles are **46-65 characters** and five were **95-116**, with
nothing in between; 70 and 75 fit the same eleven, which is what shows the gap is
real rather than a threshold picked to split the difference. Five rewritten, all
now 34-58.

### Where the cut sentence goes, and where it honestly cannot

`Shortcut` gained a `detail` field and `_tooltip_for()` shows it - **on the
`Adw.PreferencesGroup` fallback only**. `Adw.ShortcutsItem` is a **model** in both
the 1.8 and 1.9 spellings, so on the native dialog that runs here the shorter
subtitle is genuinely all the row can say. Recorded on the constant and on the
helper rather than papered over, the same way `ShortcutsWindow` already records
that `parent` is honoured by the fallback and ignored on 1.9.

**My first version called `set_tooltip_text` on both model builders.** The suite
caught it on the first run with the exact message -

    AttributeError: 'ShortcutsItem' object has no attribute 'set_tooltip_text'

- which is the module's own docstring being right ("both the section and the item
are plain models, not widgets") and me having read past it. Two of the three
builders were wrong and the third was right, which is what an unguarded
assumption about one of three shapes produces.

### Verified by rendering again, not by the test

## The render gate passed a blank page at 31%, and a frame around nothing at 14% (2026-10-13)

The `_content_percent` gate added earlier today was **itself the false pass it
was written to catch**, in two independent ways. Both were found by measuring a
real target rather than a fixture.

### Hole one: a pixel that was never painted was counted as ink

`empty` rendered and the sweep called it **PASS at 31%**. It is a blank page. The
sampler took `px[x, y][:3]`, which **drops alpha**, so the image's **62,269 fully
transparent pixels** were compared as RGB black against a background they were
never part of. Measured on the real file:

    background (248,248,248,34) x201911     the alpha-34 wash
    (0,0,0,0)              x 62269          never painted - counted as content
    (243,243,243,42)       x 17639          a delta of 5 - imperceptible

A pixel that was never painted is **not content and not background**, so `alpha
== 0` is now excluded from the population entirely. **And that is what makes
"the background" mean anything** - it is defined as the most common colour of
the *painted* pixels.

### Hole two: a delta of 5 is antialiasing, not a mark

`TOLERANCE = 8`. The cue layer's own measurement puts subpixel antialiasing
fringes at **3**, so 8 is above the noise and far below anything a person sees.
Without it, `empty`'s `(243,243,243)`-on-`(248,248,248)` counted as a page.

### The floor was not the third hole - the *shape* of the ink was

With both fixed, `empty` measures **0% and fails**, and real renders still pass.
But the `CHRONOA_FORCE_SIZE` frame around an empty main window measures **14%**
and **still clears a 5% floor**, because the rounded orange frame *is* real
high-contrast ink and the frame grows with the canvas while the interior stays
empty.

**No threshold on "how much ink" separates those**, so the question has to be
*where* the ink is. `_interior_ink()` measures the same contrast inside a 12%
margin, and the gate asks **is it zero** - a presence test with no tuned number,
because a percentage there is the wrong instrument: the real `shortcuts` window
has only **4%** interior ink and is a genuine render, so any floor would reject
it and any floor that did not would be fitted to this machine.

**Measured on every real target this repository has produced:**

| target | overall | interior ink | verdict |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| `empty` (blank page) | **0%** | **0%** | **FAIL** |
| `main` with the size override (frame only) | 14% | **0%** | **FAIL** |
| `main` at 1280x860 (frame only) | 13% | **0%** | **FAIL** |
| `main` at its own 460x640 | 17% | 10% | PASS |
| `shortcuts` (real, before the subtitle fix) | 9% | 4% | PASS |
| `shortcuts` (real, after it) | 13% | 5% | PASS |

Seven of seven correct, including the two that are false passes and the two
real renders that a naive interior *floor* would have rejected.

### Readable-and-empty is 0; unreadable is nothing

`_opaque_percent`'s rule applied to this pair of measures: an image that opened
and is entirely unpainted **is** measurable and its answer is `0`, while a
truncated file, a non-PNG or a missing Pillow prints **nothing** and the gate
**fails** it. The old gate passed all three - the same defect as a blank page
passing, because "no answer" and "no content" are not the same answer.

### 7 new tests, 5 mutations caught, 1 equivalent - and one vacuous fixture

**The fixture was broken before the code was, and running is what said so.**
`_faint_wash` used `(x + y) % 2`, and the sampler steps by **8** - so every
sampled `x` and `y` is even, `(x + y) % 2` is *always* 0, and the checkerboard
aliased into a **single flat colour**. The test passed at any tolerance
whatsoever: I set `TOLERANCE = 0` and it stayed green. `x % 3` instead, which
does not alias against an 8-step grid, and the same mutation moves it to **37%**.

**The mutation I wrote first was equivalent.** Weakening `if a == 0:` to
`if a == False:` changed nothing, because `0 == False` in Python. Deleting the
skip moves `half-transparent` from **0% to 50%**.

| mutation | result |
|---|---|
| interior measured over the whole image (the shipped false pass) | **1 failed** |
| `(( interior > 0 ))` dropped from the gate | **1 failed** |
| the `alpha == 0` skip deleted | **0% -> 50%**, fails |
| `TOLERANCE = 8` -> `0` | **0% -> 37%**, fails |
| readable-and-empty printing nothing | returns `None`, fails |
| `if a == False:` | **equivalent** - `0 == False` |

**And the driver's FAIL line finally quotes what it measured**, which is the
sentence that sent the previous four diagnoses looking for a missing file rather
than a rejected one.

### `_keep_log` paid for itself twice, in two consecutive attempts

This is the entry the `keep the diagnostic` change was made for. Two sweeps in
succession reported **`0 rendered, 2 not` with no PNG on disk**, and both causes
were named from the kept log on the **first** attempt:

    NameError: name '_count_descendants' is not defined
    AttributeError: 'TransformNode' object has no attribute 'get_n_children'

The first is the *same* defect this file recorded earlier today, and the reason
it recurred is the one that entry names: **the traceback says the call is at line
336, and on disk it is at 362 with the definition at 313** - `render_ui.py` was
**edited after the render ran**, so the helper did not exist at capture time and
does now. **An absence measured against a file being written measures the
author's progress, not the repository**, which is the `code_hl` shape and the
third time this file has hit it.

**A diagnostic nobody can read is not a diagnostic.** Four earlier attempts at
this produced nothing because the sandbox deleted the log on exit; the first
sweep after that change put a traceback on disk.

### Not claimed: the driver-level end-to-end

**The gate has not yet been shown accepting a real capture *through the driver
itself*.** `render_ui.py` is 93 insertions of another session's uncommitted work
and is currently broken in **two separate places** (`_count_descendants`
undefined, then `_node_size` calling `get_n_children()` on a `Gsk.Node`), so
every render target currently produces no file. It is theirs, the rules forbid
editing it, and fixing a capture path cannot be verified on a box where every
render is broken.

The evidence above is **the seven real PNGs scored by the driver's own extracted
functions**, plus 15 tests and 5 mutations. An end-to-end pass needs a renderer
that runs, and saying otherwise is the confident wrong answer this file has
recorded against its own harness four times.

## The rotation shipped, and the reader kept one generation of it (2026-10-13)

`tool_calls.log` is now size-capped and rotated: 16 MiB active, 8 archives, at
990 bytes a record and 764 a day. The cap was needed - the log measured
**18,914,951 bytes / 19,110 records over 25 days**, 276 MB a year, and this
repository's own `log_files` skill described it as *"still growing, and
unrotated"*. **The log is 18.9 MiB against a 16 MiB cap, so it is over the cap
before a record is written and the next `record_call()` rotates it.**

**Measured on a copy of the real file, through the real dispatch path, at the
real size** - because a code path about to run on every write should have been
run once before shipping rather than only on 40-byte fixtures.

| | |
|---|---|
| records before | 19,110 |
| records after one `record_call()` | **19,111** |
| the first 19,110 | byte-identical and in order |
| chunk modes | `tool_calls.log.1` 0600, `tool_calls.log` 0600 |
| elapsed | **0.001 s** - a rename, not a copy |

**So the retention half is clean, and the reader half - which is the half the
whole change exists for - was not.**

### The reader kept one generation, and said nothing

`learning._entries()` read an explicit path as *exactly that file*, on the
principle written into its own docstring: *"a caller naming a file is naming a
file."* **Four callers pass one and three of them pass the active log on their
own default branch** - `score_predictions` writes `_entries(log or
_log_path())`, which is the active log whenever its argument is absent.

    _entries(log) after the first rotation  ->  1 record of 19,111

Nothing reported that 19,110 had gone. **The absence-shaped wrong answer this
change was written to prevent, arrived through the change**, and the reader that
most needed the history was reading one generation of it - `score_predictions`,
whose own docstring calls itself *"the live check that calibration holds on calls
the model had not seen when it was fitted"*.

`_durable_records()` had it right already, a few hundred lines above in the same
file, with no explicit-path branch to get wrong. **Two readers of one file
disagreeing about what the file is, is what said so** - the disagreement, not
either one of them, and not the test suite.

### The mutation I believed was a defect was the fix

The set carried `a caller naming one file gets the whole archive set`, with one
witness and the same reasoning in its `why`. It is now the shipped behaviour, so
it is **deleted**, and its inverse is the mutation. A mutation that reproduces the
fix is not a mutation. The witness it cited survived it *correctly*: a path with
no archives beside it **is** one file - which is why that test is still true, and
why its class is renamed `TestANamedPathWithNoArchivesIsOneFile`. **A stale name
on a passing test reads as coverage of a property nobody is asserting.**

### Two more readers, and the end-to-end test is what found the third

`dream` had its **own** `_entries`: a byte-for-byte copy of
`learning._entries_of`, reading one file - which a source scan for `_entries(`
reads as the same name. `dream.read_log` opened one file too, so the counter and
the data disagreed (**3 archived + 3 fresh gave `read_log` 6 and `_entries` 3**)
and `dream()`'s own reconciliation line **rewrote the count to 3 rather than
reporting the disagreement**. A consolidation pass announced a fraction of the
history as the whole of it.

The duplicate parser is now a delegation - two implementations of "parse this
log's records" is how `wpctl` ended up in three modules and the finite check in
four - and `read_log`'s byte budget is spent newest-first *across the whole
history*, with its own two over-fix mutations, because reading every chunk is
only correct while something still bounds it.

### Four tests that could not fail, all found by running them

- **`record_call`'s third positional is `result`, not `verdict`.** The test
  helper's `"ok"` has been landing there all along, so every record that file
  wrote carried `verdict: None` - harmless for count and order, wrong for
  anything reading verdicts, and it failed two of the new tests before the
  signature was read. The trap is now in the helper's docstring.
- **The byte budget's limit was typed** - 400 against ~200 bytes a record is less
  than the three records just written, so the budget cut *inside* the newest
  chunk and the test reported "2 of 3". Correct code, wrong expectation, and the
  same off-by-a-handful mistake as the rotation bounds. Derived from the file now.
- **The calibration witness asserted the argument, not the value** - a wiring
  assertion. The runner named it and reported "NOT caught by", which is right.
- **The dream report named neither chunk** because both tools' calls verified, so
  `analyse` correctly said *"nothing stands out"*.

### And five mutations had been printing "NOT caught by" on every run

Correcting the defect exposed the set's own bookkeeping: eight names across five
mutations could not bite, and **all eight were wrong rather than missing**. Two
worth carrying: `test_a_write_below_the_cap_does_not_rotate` asserts a small
write does **not** rotate, and with the size check deleted nothing ever rotates -
same outcome, green with the defect. **A guard that can only fail in one
direction needs the other direction's mutation to be seen at all**, which is why
two mutations now share one witness rather than having two that do not
discriminate. And one name was listed twice, so a single witness was standing in
for two and the count was padding. Every replacement was already in the runner's
`also:` line - *correct the name, do not write a new test*.

37 tests. 17 mutations, **16 caught, 1 equivalent (documented), 0 survivors, 0
unmeasurable, 0 stale**, and no line reading "NOT caught by". 284 passed across
the rotation, learning, dream, distill and outcome-model suites.

## The empty state had the capability signal, and 187px of it was below the fold (2026-10-13)

Asked to make the empty composer capability-driven - "a Try asking row built
from `available_surfaces()`". **It is already there**, and measuring it before
building it is the whole entry.

`SuggestionBar` has been in the empty state throughout. `show_placeholder()`
adds three rows: the prompt, a dim line of shortcut hints, and the bar. The bar
is built from `capabilities.startup_suggestions(self._caps)`, which is filtered
against the live registry, so a skill that is not loaded is never offered; and
clicking **fills** the composer rather than sending, which the module's own
docstring gives as the reason. Real window, its own 460x640:

```
[0] h=  18  Ask something, or press the orb to speak
[1] h=  37  Ctrl+K for anything else  ·  Ctrl+F to find...  ·  ? for what...
[2] h=294  SuggestionBar

empty state total  : 349px
transcript viewport: 162px
-> DOES NOT FIT, over by 187px
```

**So the premise is wrong and the conclusion is right.** The signal was built,
correct and registry-derived - and invisible, which reads exactly like absent.
The chips were also on six rows while using 199/134/201/272/243/149px of a ~380px
column: two fitted per row and GTK gave one each.

### The fix is the mode strip's own rule, applied to a chip

`SUGGESTION_WORDS` holds a **name** per prompt - `Battery left?`, `Which
model?`, `Search the web` - keyed by the full question, so the registry gate is
untouched and a prompt can only be shortened if the skill that owns it really
loaded. The chip prints the name; the tooltip, the accessible name and the click
payload all carry the question in full.

This is **"a menu item is a name, not a sentence"** arriving in a third widget,
for the same reason and with the same consequence: a chip renders `label` and
nothing beside it, so it can only hold a label. And it is safe only because of
the property that already existed - the click **fills**, so the person reads the
full question in the composer and can edit it before it goes anywhere.

After, same window, same probe: **149px in 162px, FITS**, two rows of three
(chips 104-132px).

### 5 mutations, 5 caught - and the first survivor was a test that never reached the product

Reverting the one line where the transcript passes the table **left all 31
tests green**, because every test in the new file built a `SuggestionBar`
directly and never touched `TranscriptView.show_placeholder()`. That is this
file's own *"a test that reaches past the call site to the function behind it is
testing the function"*, and it is the whole defect - the widget right, the
product unchanged. `test_the_empty_state_itself_prints_the_names` builds the real
window; that mutation now fails.

| mutation | caught by |
|---|---|
| the chip sends its short word instead of the question | 2 |
| a word dropped from the table (chip goes long again) | 2 |
| **the transcript stops passing the table** | **1 - and 0 before the product test** |
| the empty-state scroll fix restored (ships as it was) | 1 |
| the over-fix - always scroll to the top | 1 |

The last two are the `_apply_follow` fix that had been sitting uncommitted and
untested from earlier today, so it is in the same commit rather than shipped on
trust. Its motivating measurement was the **375px in a 201px** overflow this
entry's own change largely removes; the rule it encodes still stands, and
`_sized()` sets the adjustment explicitly because an unallocated view reports
`upper == page_size == 0` and would make "followed to the bottom" and "scrolled
to the top" indistinguishable.

### Three of my own errors, each recorded because each looked like the product

- **Two existing tests failed on correct code.** `test_ui_surfaces` derived the
  expected question from the chip's *visible* label - true only while label and

**Not claimed: a pixel test.** The behaviour is asserted without a display; the
